definition_zh: 标准；水准；标准的
definition_en: a rule or measure used to judge quality, a level of quality, or the usual accepted type
core_image: 一把用来衡量长度的尺子
scene: 这家旅馆达到很高的标准。 The hotel meets a high standard.
sceneCN: 这里 standard 是「标准」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家旅馆达到很高的标准。

senses.title: Rule for judging
senses.definition: a rule or measure used to judge quality or correctness
senses.definitionCN: 用来评判质量或正确性的规则或尺度
senses.example: The hotel meets a high standard.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆达到很高的标准。
senses.why: A rule for judging quality is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 衡量质量的规则，是这个词的核心义项。

senses.title: Level reached
senses.definition: the level of quality that someone or something reaches
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所达到的质量水平
senses.example: Her work is above the average standard.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作高于一般水准。
senses.why: The measured level grew from the rule itself.
senses.whyCN: 被衡量的水准，由规则本身引申而来。

senses.title: Usual type
senses.definition: of the usual or accepted type, not special
senses.definitionCN: 属于通常或公认类型的，非特殊的
senses.example: This is the standard model.
senses.exampleCN: 这是标准型号。
senses.why: Anything of the accepted type is called standard.
senses.whyCN: 凡属公认类型的事物，都称作标准的。

intro.en: Standard came through Old French from a Germanic compound meaning to stand firmly.
intro.cn: standard 经古法语而来，源头是意为「稳稳站立」的日耳曼语复合词。

items.en: A compound meant standing firmly.
items.cn: 一个复合词意为稳稳站立。

items.en: Estandard named a flag raised as a rallying sign.
items.cn: estandard 指挥舞起来集结人马的旗帜。

items.en: Standard meant a flag and then a fixed measure.
items.cn: standard 先指旗帜，后指固定的度量。

items.en: It named an accepted rule for judging quality.
items.cn: 它指评判质量的公认规则。

items.en: The adjective sense of usual type appeared.
items.cn: 「通常类型」的形容词义随之出现。

note.en: Standard is compared with look-alike words and words for measures of quality.
note.cn: 把 standard 与形近词以及表示质量尺度的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Standard is a rule that measures quality, the level reached, and the usual type.
normalIntro.cn: standard 是衡量质量的规则，是达到的水准，也是常规的类型。

normal.en: The hotel meets a high standard.

normal.en: Her work is above the average standard.

normal.en: This is the standard model.

normal.en: By any standard, the result is good.
normal.cn: 无论按什么标准，结果都不错。

abstract.en: A ruler turns length into a judgement.
abstract.cn: 一把尺子，把长度变成判断。

abstract.en: A level reached becomes a level expected.
abstract.cn: 达到的水准，变成期待的水准。

abstract.en: What most people accept becomes standard.
abstract.cn: 多数人接受的，就成了标准。

root: 经古法语 estandard（军旗）源于日耳曼语「稳稳站立」的复合词；从集结人马的旗帜，引申为公认的度量与评判规则。

sensesIntro.en: Standard means a rule for judging, the level reached, or the usual accepted type.

core.en: A fixed measure for judging.
core.cn: 用于评判的固定尺度。

branches.en: A ruler lies beside the cloth.

branches.en: A needle marks the level reached.

branches.en: An ordinary product leaves the factory.

branches.en: The rule and the level it measures belong together.

branches.en: The level people expect becomes the usual type.

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic by way of Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，是经古法语而来的日耳曼语词。

items.meaning: a flag or a fixed measure
items.example: The flag was the king's standard.

definition_zh: 极好的；了不起的；幻想的；奇异的；（数量）大得惊人的
definition_en: extraordinarily good, imaginary, bizarre, or impossibly large
core_image: 烟花在夜空炸开成不存在的花，围观的人齐声喊出同一个赞叹词
scene: 科学展上机器人完成了高难动作，全班同学一起欢呼鼓掌。 The robot's dance was fantastic, and the whole class cheered.
sceneCN: 这里指「极好的」，对应第 1 个义项：好得超出寻常；句意为机器人的舞蹈太精彩了，全班都欢呼。画面要点：机器人、展台、鼓掌的同学们。

pos.zh: 极好的；幻想的；奇异的；大得惊人的

derivatives.zh: 幻想（同根名词：心中显现的影像）
难以置信地；极好地（副词形式）

幻影（同根异路词：希腊语经拉丁语进入英语）

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: extraordinarily good or attractive
senses.definitionCN: 特别好或特别吸引人
senses.example: The party was fantastic.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会棒极了。
senses.why: Daily speech borrowed the exaggeration of imagination as praise.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语借来想象的夸张当赞美。

senses.title: Imaginary or unreal
senses.definition: based on imagination rather than reality
senses.definitionCN: 基于想象而非现实
senses.example: The novel is set in a fantastic kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说设定在一个幻想王国。
senses.why: The original Greek sense: what appears only in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原义：只在心中显现之物。

senses.title: Strangely shaped or extravagant
senses.definition: strange, extravagant, or bizarre in form
senses.definitionCN: 外形奇异、铺张或怪诞
senses.example: Fantastic towers crowned the palace.
senses.exampleCN: 怪异的塔楼耸立在宫殿上。
senses.why: What imagination builds often looks strange to plain eyes.
senses.whyCN: 想象所造之物，在朴素眼光里往往显得怪异。

senses.title: Impossibly large in amount
senses.definition: so large that it seems unreal
senses.definitionCN: 大到仿佛不真实
senses.example: He was offered a fantastic sum.
senses.exampleCN: 有人给他一笔大得惊人的款项。
senses.why: Numbers beyond belief are numbers from a fantasy.
senses.whyCN: 大到难以置信的数字，是从幻想里来的数字。

intro.en: Fantastic goes back to Greek phantastikos, 'able to present to the mind', from phainesthai, 'to appear'.
intro.cn: fantastic 回溯希腊语 phantastikos（能在心中呈现的），出自 phainesthai（显现）。

items.en: Greek phantastikos described images that appear in the mind; phantasia meant appearance or imagination.
items.cn: 希腊语 phantastikos 描述心中显现的影像；phantasia 意为显现或想象。

items.en: Latin phantasticus borrowed the word for imaginary, spectral things.
items.cn: 拉丁语 phantasticus 借入该词，指想象中的、如幻影般的事物。

items.en: Old French fantastique carried the word toward England.
items.cn: 古法语 fantastique 把该词送往英格兰。

items.en: Middle English fantastic meant existing only in imagination, often with a hint of absurdity.
items.cn: 中古英语 fantastic 意为只存在于想象之中，常带荒诞意味。

items.en: Modern English split the word: imaginative in art criticism, 'excellent' in everyday speech.
items.cn: 现代英语让该词分岔：艺术批评中指「富于想象」，日常口语指「极好」。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin root phant- (what appears); near-meaning words name degrees of excellence and imagination.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 phant-（显现之物）；近义组命名「极好」的程度与想象之域。

entries.definition: a ghost, an appearance without substance
entries.definitionCN: 幻影；同根异路，保留 ph- 拼法

entries.definition: imaginary rather than real
entries.definitionCN: 富于想象的；词源为 fancy，与 fantastic 相互影响但不同源

entries.definition: surprisingly good

entries.definition: very good
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；语气稍缓

entries.definition: hard to believe, often in a good way

normalIntro.en: Five grips on a Greek word for what appears in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 希腊语「心中显现之物」，五个抓手。

normal.en: fantastic and fantasy share the Greek root for what appears in the mind.
normal.cn: fantastic 与 fantasy 共享希腊语「心中显现」的词根。

normal.en: Everyday speech uses fantastic as the strongest everyday praise: fantastic idea, fantastic view.
normal.cn: 日常口语把 fantastic 当最强的称赞：fantastic idea、fantastic view。

normal.en: phantom keeps the ph- spelling of the same Greek root.
normal.cn: phantom 保留同一希腊词根的 ph- 拼法。

normal.en: Fantastic Beasts put the old 'imaginary' sense in a title.
normal.cn: 《神奇动物》（Fantastic Beasts）把旧的「想象」义放进了片名。

normal.en: a fantastic sum means an amount too big to seem real.
normal.cn: a fantastic sum 指大到不像真实存在的金额。

abstract.en: Imagination is a projector; fantastic is the light it throws.
abstract.cn: 想象是放映机；fantastic 是它投出的光。

abstract.en: Praise is exaggeration domesticated: fantastic tames wonder into a compliment.
abstract.cn: 赞美是被驯化的夸张：fantastic 把惊叹驯成一句恭维。

abstract.en: What appears only in the mind casts the longest shadow on paper.
abstract.cn: 只在心中显现之物，在纸上投下最长的影子。

examples.en: You did a fantastic job on the project.
examples.cn: 你在这个项目上做得太出色了。

examples.en: The story takes place in a fantastic world of talking animals.
examples.cn: 故事发生在一个动物会说话的幻想世界。

examples.en: They paid a fantastic price for the small flat.
examples.cn: 他们为这套小公寓付了高得离谱的价钱。

sensesIntro.en: From mind-born images outward to praise, strangeness, and impossible size.

branches.en: THE BIZARRE: what imagination builds looks strange.

branches.en: THE IMMENSE: amounts that seem unreal.

definition_zh: 总的；总计的；完全的；全部；总数；合计达
definition_en: the whole amount of something, or complete and entire, or to add up to a figure
core_image: 一长串账单被最后一道横线压住，末尾写着一个整整齐齐的数
scene: 结账时收银条一路打印到纸尾，最下面那一行加粗。 The total for the trip came to more than we had planned.
sceneCN: 这里 total 是「总数、总额」（第 4 个义项：所有部分相加之和）；句意为这趟旅行的总额超出了我们的计划。画面里有长条小票、最末那行加粗的数字。

pos.zh: 形容词：总的；全部的；完全的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「完全地；全部地」
加 -ity 构成，义为「整体；全部」
加前缀 sub- 构成，义为「小计；部分合计」
由 total 派生的政治术语，义为「极权的」

senses.title: The whole amount
senses.definition: the complete amount obtained by adding all the parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分相加所得的完整数量
senses.example: The total of the two bills was surprisingly small.
senses.exampleCN: 两张账单的总额小得令人意外。
senses.why: The Latin word for the whole is the direct source, so the noun names the sum in its completeness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「整体」的词是直接来源，故名词指完整加总后的量。

senses.title: Adding up to a figure
senses.definition: to amount to a particular figure when all parts are counted
senses.definitionCN: 各部分组成加总起来达到某个数字
senses.example: The costs totalled more than three thousand yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 这些花费合计超过三千元。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to make a total out of scattered items.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把零散的项加总成一个总数。

senses.title: Complete and absolute
senses.definition: used of something with no part missing or no exception allowed
senses.definitionCN: 用于毫无缺失或毫无例外的情形
senses.example: The room fell into total silence when she began to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 她开口时，屋子里一片死寂。
senses.why: If a total is everything, then a total silence is silence without one sound left out.
senses.whyCN: 既然总数意味着全部，那么 total silence 就是一点声音也没遗漏的静。

senses.title: A sum of money owed
senses.definition: the full sum due for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 为货物或服务应付的全部款项
senses.example: Please pay the total within seven days of the invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 请在开票后七天内付清总额。
senses.why: Shops print the total at the bottom of a receipt, since it is the last and whole figure.
senses.whyCN: 商店把小票底部的那个数叫作 total，因为它是最后也是完整的那个数。

senses.title: Counting everything in
senses.definition: including every member or part, as in the total number of students
senses.definitionCN: 包括每个成员或每个部分，如学生总人数
senses.example: The total number of students rose by two hundred this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年学生总人数增加了两百。
senses.why: The adjective marks a count that leaves nothing outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记一种不把任何东西留在外面的计数。

senses.title: A whole in philosophy
senses.definition: in older philosophical writing, the whole made of parts that hang together
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的哲学文字中，指由相联部分构成的整体
senses.example: The old textbook speaks of the total as more than the sum of its parts.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧教材说整体大于其各部分之和。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the word for any whole that holds together, which is the root idea unextended.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用这个词指任何自成一体的整体，这正是未加引申的词根本义。

senses.title: Complete ruin in expressions
senses.definition: used in phrases such as a total loss to mean damage beyond recovery
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a total loss 等短语，表示彻底损失、无法挽回
senses.example: The storm left the boat a total loss.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴使那条船彻底报废。
senses.why: Insurance language needs a word for damage with nothing left to save, and total supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 保险用语需要一个词表示无可挽回的损毁，total 正好提供。

senses.title: Everything considered
senses.definition: used in phrases like in total or a total of to introduce a final count
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in total 或 a total of 等短语引出最终计数
senses.example: A total of forty people signed the sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 共有四十人在表上签了字。
senses.why: The phrase works like a bracket around a list, closing it with one figure.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语像一对括号把一串项目包起来，再用一个数字收尾。

intro.en: Total comes from medieval Latin totalis, an adjective from totus, the Latin word for whole or entire, and it entered English through French.
intro.cn: total 来自中世纪拉丁语 totalis，是 totus（意为「整个、全部」）的形容词，经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Totus means all, whole, or entire, and it has no parts to be counted separately.
items.cn: 拉丁语 totus 意为「全部、整个」，它本身不再被拆成可数的部分。

items.en: The derived adjective totalis names what belongs to the whole rather than to a part.
items.cn: 由它派生的形容词 totalis 指属于整体而非属于部分的。

items.en: Old French takes total as an adjective of the schools and of accounts.
items.cn: 古法语把 total 用作学校与账目中的形容词。

items.en: Middle English borrows the adjective and soon uses it as a noun for the sum.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个形容词，很快又把它用作表示总和的名称。

items.en: The verb to total appears in the eighteenth century in bookkeeping and in arithmetic.
items.cn: 动词 total 于十八世纪出现在簿记与算术中。

items.en: The emphatic sense of complete, as in total silence, spreads in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 表示「完全」的强调义（如 total silence）在十九、二十世纪扩散开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for sums and for completeness.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干的形式，近义组则汇集表示总和与完整性的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories use the fixed phrases in total and a total of, the bookkeeping verb, and the emphatic use with abstract nouns.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用 in total 与 a total of 的固定搭配、簿记中的动词用法，以及与抽象名词连用时的强调用法。

normal.en: In total and a total of both close a list with one figure.
normal.cn: in total 与 a total of 都用同一个数字为一串项目收尾。

normal.en: A total loss is insurance language, and it means nothing can be saved.
normal.cn: a total loss 是保险用语，意思是无可挽救。

normal.en: The verb is written totalled in British spelling and totaled in American spelling.
normal.cn: 动词在英式拼写中写作 totalled，美式写作 totaled。

normal.en: Total silence means no sound at all, which shows how the word moves from sums to absolutes.
normal.cn: total silence 指一点声音也没有，这显示该词如何从加总走向绝对。

normal.en: Subtotal takes the prefix sub- and gives the sum below the main one.
normal.cn: subtotal 加前缀 sub-，给出主总额之下的那个小计。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures and a single line ruled under the last of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字，最后一行下面划着一道横线。

abstract.en: Think of an empty room where even the echo has stopped.
abstract.cn: 想一间空房，连回声都停了。

abstract.en: A total leaves nothing outside it, whether it counts money or measures silence.
abstract.cn: 总数不把任何东西留在外面，无论它数的是钱，还是衡量的是静。

examples.en: In total, the project took eleven months to finish.
examples.cn: 这个项目总共用了十一个月才完成。

examples.en: He was in total agreement with the plan.
examples.cn: 他完全同意这个计划。

examples.en: The company's sales totalled nearly two million units last year.
examples.cn: 去年公司的销量合计接近两百万台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「头托」——把所有数一起托到头上，就是总数 total。

root: 拉丁语 totus（全部、整个）→ 中世纪拉丁语 totalis → 古法语 total → 英语 total。同族词有 totality、subtotal；totus 还与 totidem（同样多）同源。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the added-up sum, then follows the same whole into the verbs of counting, the adjective of completeness, and the emphatic phrases of absolute loss or silence.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从加总求和开始，再沿「整体」这一概念走入计数的动词、表示完整的形容词，以及「彻底损失」「彻底寂静」这类强调短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole closed by a ruled line.
core.cn: 核心意象：被一道横线封住的整体。

branches.en: The sum itself and the phrases that present it.
branches.cn: 总和本身以及呈现它的短语。

branches.en: The act of adding parts into a figure.
branches.cn: 把各部分加成一个数字的动作。

branches.en: Completeness and the total count.
branches.cn: 完整性与全部计数。

branches.en: The philosophical whole.
branches.cn: 哲学意义上的整体。

branches.en: Total loss as damage with nothing left.
branches.cn: 彻底损失指无可挽回的损毁。

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective used as noun, verb, and adjective; its family comes from -ly, -ity, and the prefix sub-.
intro.cn: 本词是兼作名词、动词与形容词的拉丁源形容词，其词族来自 -ly、-ity 与前缀 sub-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give totus and the words formed beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出 totus 及其旁生的词。

items.example: The form is unchanged from Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式自拉丁语以来未变。

items.example: Totus is the source of the stem.
items.exampleCN: totus 是这个词干的来源。

items.example: Totally means in a complete way.
items.exampleCN: totally 意为以完全的方式。

items.example: Totality is the state of being whole.
A subtotal is a sum below the main one.
items.exampleCN: subtotal 是主总额之下的小计。

items.example: Totalling the column took a minute.
items.exampleCN: 把那一列加总用了一分钟。

definition_zh: 基本的；基础的；简单的；基本知识；碱性的
definition_en: forming the base or most necessary part of something
core_image: 一座房子的地基埋在土里，上面的墙都靠它
scene: 上课前，老师先在黑板上写下三条最基本的规则。 The teacher explained the basic rules before the game started.
sceneCN: 这里 basic 是「基本的」（第 1 个义项：构成基础、最必要的）；句意为比赛开始前老师讲解了基本规则。

pos.zh: 形容词：基本的；基础的；简单的；碱性的
名词：基本知识（常用复数）

derivatives.zh: 由 basic 加 -ally 构成，义为「基本上；大体上」
由 basic 加 -s 构成，义为「基本知识；基础」
基础词，义为「底部；基础」，basic 由它加后缀构成
与 base 同源的拉丁借词，义为「基础；根据」

senses.title: Fundamental
senses.definition: forming the base or the most necessary part of something
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物的基础或最必要部分
senses.example: The teacher explained the basic rules before the game.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前老师讲解了基本规则。
senses.why: The word is built on base, so the first sense is whatever sits under everything else and holds it up.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 base 之上，所以第一义就是垫在下面、支撑其余部分的东西。

senses.title: Simple, not advanced
senses.definition: simple and at an early level, without extra details
senses.definitionCN: 简单、处于初级水平，不带额外细节
senses.example: This book uses basic English for new readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书用简单的英语面向初学者。
senses.why: What is at the base comes before anything advanced, so basic also means the plain early level.
senses.whyCN: 处在底部的东西先于一切高级内容，所以 basic 也表示朴素的初级层次。

senses.title: Necessary for living
senses.definition: needed by everyone as a minimum for a decent life
senses.definitionCN: 人人过像样生活所需的最低条件
senses.example: Clean water is a basic need for every family.
senses.exampleCN: 干净的水是每个家庭的基本需求。
senses.why: If something is the base of life, it cannot be left out, which gives the sense of a minimum necessity.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物是生活的地基，就不能缺少，于是有了「最低必需」的义项。

senses.title: The essential facts
senses.definition: the simple, essential facts or skills of a subject, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某学科最简单、最必要的事实或技能，常用复数
senses.example: She taught me the basics of cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 她教了我烹饪的基本知识。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the things that form the base of a skill.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指构成某项技能之基础的那些内容。

senses.title: Alkaline
senses.definition: having the chemical properties of a base rather than an acid
senses.definitionCN: 具有碱而非酸的化学性质
senses.example: Soap is basic, so it can hurt your eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 肥皂是碱性的，所以可能刺激眼睛。
senses.why: Chemistry uses base for an alkaline substance, and the adjective basic follows that technical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 化学用 base 指碱，形容词 basic 就沿用了这个专业含义。

intro.en: Basic is an English adjective built on base, which goes back through French to Latin and Greek.
intro.cn: basic 是建立在 base 之上的英语形容词，base 经法语上溯到拉丁语与希腊语。

items.en: Greek basis meant a step or a pedestal, from bainein, to go.
items.cn: 希腊语 basis 指台阶或基座，来自 bainein「走」。

items.en: Latin basis kept the sense of a foundation and also gave the word for a chemical base.
items.cn: 拉丁语 basis 保留「基础」之义，也给出了化学中「碱」的名称。

items.en: English base arrives through Old French and means the bottom part that supports something.
items.cn: 英语 base 经古法语而来，指支撑某物的底部。

items.en: The adjective basic is formed by adding the Greek-derived suffix -ic to base.
items.cn: 形容词 basic 由 base 加上源自希腊语的后缀 -ic 构成。

items.en: The chemical sense is recorded in the nineteenth century, and the everyday sense of fundamental spreads in the twentieth.
items.cn: 化学义在十九世纪有记录，日常的「根本」义则在二十世纪广泛使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base family; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is fundamental, simple, or essential.
note.cn: 形近组收 base 词族；近义组收表示根本、简单与必需的词。

entries.definition: The bottom part that supports something, or a main substance in chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「底部；基础；碱」，是 basic 的基础词。

entries.definition: In the main, in the simplest important respect.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「基本上、大体上」，由 basic 加 -ally 构成。

entries.definition: The simplest and most necessary facts or skills.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「基本知识、基础」，由 basic 加 -s 构成。

entries.definition: A round open container for water; it comes from a different Latin word and only looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「盆、水池」；只是拼写相近，词源来自另一个拉丁词，与 base 无关。

entries.definition: Forming the necessary centre of a system; stronger and more formal than basic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「根本的、基础的」，比 basic 更强调核心且更正式。

entries.definition: Absolutely necessary; it stresses need rather than level.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「必不可少的」，强调必要性而非层次。

entries.definition: At the simplest level of a subject; close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「初级的、基本的」，对应第二个义项。

entries.definition: Easy to understand or do, with nothing extra.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「简单的」，强调不复杂、无多余部分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real base root, the suffix -ic, and the fixed phrases the adjective appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的 base 词根、后缀 -ic，以及这个形容词的固定搭配。

normal.en: Basic is base plus -ic, and a base is what everything else stands on.
normal.cn: basic 是 base 加 -ic，而 base 正是其他一切所站立之处。

normal.en: Basic English uses only simple words, which shows the second sense.
normal.cn: Basic English 只用简单词汇，体现第二个义项。

normal.en: Basic needs are food, water, and shelter, the minimum for life.
normal.cn: basic needs 是食物、水和住所，是生活的最低条件。

normal.en: The basics of a subject are what a beginner must learn first.
normal.cn: 一门学科的 basics 是初学者必须先学的内容。

normal.en: In chemistry a base is the opposite of an acid, so basic means alkaline.
normal.cn: 化学中 base 是酸的对立面，所以 basic 表示「碱性的」。

abstract.en: Picture a house: the walls and roof are visible, but only the buried foundation makes them possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子：墙和屋顶看得见，但真正撑住它们的却是埋在地下的地基。

abstract.en: Remove the foundation and the house falls, just as a skill collapses without its basics.
abstract.cn: 抽掉地基房子就倒，正如技能失去基础就崩塌。

abstract.en: The same word covers a beginner's level and a chemical property, because both are starting points.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指初学水平，也能指化学性质，因为两者都是「起点」。

examples.en: The teacher explained the basic rules before the game started.
examples.cn: 比赛开始前老师讲解了基本规则。

examples.en: This book uses basic English for new readers.
examples.cn: 这本书用简单的英语面向初学者。

examples.en: She taught me the basics of cooking.
examples.cn: 她教了我烹饪的基本知识。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「背此刻」——背下此刻的要点，才算打好基础：基本的

root: basic 由 base 加后缀 -ic 构成。base 经古法语来自拉丁语 basis，源头为希腊语 basis「台阶、基座」，来自动词 bainein「走」。故「基本的」义来自「垫在底下的基座」，化学中 base 又指「碱」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of basic all come from the image of a foundation: what supports everything, the simple early level, the minimum for life, the essential facts, and the chemical starting substance.
sensesIntro.cn: basic 的五个义项都来自「地基」意象：支撑一切的部分、朴素的初级层次、生活的最低条件、必备的基本知识，以及化学上的碱性物质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone foundation sits under a house, and every wall rests on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座房子的石基埋在下面，每一面墙都压在它上面。

branches.en: THE FOUNDATION: whatever holds the rest up is basic.
branches.cn: 地基线：凡是撑住其余部分的东西，就是 basic。

branches.en: THE LEVEL: what comes before advanced work is the simple early level.
branches.cn: 层次线：先于高级内容出现的，就是朴素的初级层次。

branches.en: THE MINIMUM: the base of a decent life cannot be left out.
branches.cn: 最低线：像样生活的地基不能缺少。

branches.en: THE FACTS: the essentials of a skill are its foundation in noun form.
branches.cn: 知识线：一项技能的要领，就是它名词形式的地基。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY: a base is the starting substance that neutralizes an acid.
branches.cn: 化学线：碱是能中和酸的起始物质。

intro.en: Basic is a Latin-derived base plus a Greek-derived adjective suffix, with ordinary English endings on top.
intro.cn: basic 是拉丁来源的 base 加希腊来源的形容词后缀，再叠加普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin basis is recorded and is the direct ancestor of base; the Greek form behind it is also recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 basis 有文献记录，是 base 的直接祖先；它背后的希腊语形式同样有记录。

items.example: The base of the statue is made of stone.
items.exampleCN: 雕像的底座是石头做的。
它由 base 构成 basic。

items.example: It forms basal, meaning at the base.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 basal，意为「基部的」。
它由 basic 构成 basically。

items.example: The basics are easy to learn.
The report rests on a firm basis.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告建立在稳固的基础上。

items.example: The basal leaves lie flat on the ground.
items.exampleCN: 基部的叶子平贴在地面上。

items.example: The plan is basically the same.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划基本上是一样的。

latinEntries.meaning: the starting substance that neutralizes an acid
latinEntries.meaningCN: 碱；能与酸中和的起始物质

definition_zh: 在哪里；往哪里；在…的地方；在某一点上
definition_en: used to ask about a place, or to introduce the place in or to which something happens
core_image: 手指按在地图上的一个点，指甲下面露出一点颜色
scene: 两个人对着地图，有人用手指按住某一小块地方，抬头问。 Do you know where the key is?
sceneCN: 这里 where 是「在哪里」（第 1 个义项：询问地点）；句意为你知不知道钥匙在哪儿？手指按在地图上那一点就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 你从哪里来；你是哪儿人

senses.title: In or to what place
senses.definition: used to ask about a place or the direction of movement
senses.definitionCN: 询问地点或移动的方向
senses.example: Do you know where the key is?
senses.exampleCN: 你知不知道钥匙在哪儿？
senses.why: This is the base function of the word, and every other sense either points at a place or moves along it.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最基本的功能，其余含义或指向某处，或沿某处移动。

senses.title: In the place that
senses.definition: used to introduce a clause naming a place, usually the place of the main action
senses.definitionCN: 引出一个指明地点的从句，通常是主句动作发生的地方
senses.example: Put the box where the children cannot reach it.
senses.exampleCN: 把箱子放在孩子够不到的地方。
senses.why: A question inside a sentence keeps its place meaning but loses its question mark.
senses.whyCN: 嵌在句中的问句保留地点含义，却失去了问号。

senses.title: The place at which
senses.definition: used after a place noun to introduce the description of that place
senses.definitionCN: 用在表示地点的名词后，引出对该地点的描述
senses.example: This is the village where she grew up.
senses.exampleCN: 这就是她长大的村子。
senses.why: Once the place is already named by a noun, where only carries it into the clause.
senses.whyCN: 地点一旦已由名词点明，where 只需把它带进从句。

senses.title: In the respect that
senses.definition: used in formal writing to point at a part or a respect rather than a physical place
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式文字，指向某一方面或某一环节而不是物理地点
senses.example: The plan has one fault where the cost is concerned.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划在花费方面有一个毛病。
senses.why: Place talk widens into abstract ground, so a subject or a paragraph can also be a where.
senses.whyCN: 地点的说法扩大到抽象的立足点，于是一个话题或一段文字也可以是一个 where。

intro.en: Where comes from Old English hwær, the place adverb built on the same hwa- stem as who, what and when.
intro.cn: where 源自古英语 hwær，是建立在 who、what、when 同一 hwa- 词干上的地点副词。

items.en: The stem hwa- had a place member whose sound ended in an r, and that r is all that distinguishes where from what.
items.cn: hwa- 词干有一支表地点，其音以 r 收尾，这个 r 就是 where 与 what 的全部差别。

items.en: Hwær asked about place in both questions and clauses, and its relatives hwider and hwæder covered motion.
items.cn: hwær 在问句与从句中问地点，其相关形式 hwider 与 hwæder 负责运动方向。

items.en: The spelling became where, and English also gained whence for from where.
items.cn: 拼写变为 where，英语另有 whence 表示「从何处」。

items.en: The relative use grew beside the question use, giving sentences like the house where we lived.
items.cn: 关系用法在疑问用法旁边成长，产生了 the house where we lived 这样的句子。

items.en: Formal prose extended the word to abstract points, as in where the cost is concerned.
items.cn: 正式文字把这个词扩展到抽象的点上，如 where the cost is concerned。

note.en: The first group gathers the other wh words and place words, the second the words for place and for direction of travel.
note.cn: 第一组收其他 wh 词与地点词，第二组收表示地点与行进方向的说法。

entries.definition: The time version of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干的时间版

entries.definition: Whereas began as where plus so, and now contrasts clauses.
entries.definitionCN: whereas 本是 where 加 so，现在用于对比从句

entries.definition: Any place at all.
entries.definitionCN: 无论在哪里

entries.definition: The past of be, which looks almost identical.
entries.definitionCN: be 的过去式，外形几乎一样

entries.definition: The thing that where asks about.
entries.definitionCN: 地方

entries.definition: To what place, the old motion form, now literary.
entries.definitionCN: 往何处（旧用法，现多书面）

entries.definition: From what place, the old source form.
entries.definitionCN: 从何处

entries.definition: In a place not named, the vague answer to where.
entries.definitionCN: 在某处

normalIntro.en: Where has the r of a finger pointing, and everything in its family keeps that r.
normalIntro.cn: where 里有一个像用手指指的 r，词族里的词都保留着它。

normal.en: Where, here, there: the same -ere, ending in a place that is either asked or shown.
normal.cn: where、here、there：同样的 -ere，结尾或是问的地点，或是指出的地点。

normal.en: Wh- keeps the question; here and there are the two answers.
normal.cn: wh- 保留疑问，here 与 there 就是两种答案。

normal.en: Where is never were, though on paper the two are one letter apart in sound.
normal.cn: where 不是 were，尽管读音上两者只差一点。

normal.en: Somewhere, nowhere, anywhere: the same stem with a lid on top.
normal.cn: somewhere、nowhere、anywhere：同一个词干，上面加了不同的盖。

normal.en: In formal writing a where can mean a point in an argument, not only on a map.
normal.cn: 在正式文字中，where 可指论证中的一点，而不只地图上的位置。

abstract.en: Feel a fingertip on a folding map.
abstract.cn: 感觉指尖按在折叠地图上。

abstract.en: See a box put up high, out of reach.
abstract.cn: 看一只箱子被放到高处，够不到。

abstract.en: Hear your own village named out loud.
abstract.cn: 听别人念出你长大的村子。

examples.en: Where did you put the tickets?
examples.cn: 你把票放哪儿了？

examples.en: This is the street where my grandmother lived.
examples.cn: 这就是我祖母住过的那条街。

examples.en: Where possible, the report avoids technical words.
examples.cn: 在可能的地方，这份报告避免使用术语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔」——威尔按着地图问：我到哪儿了？

root: 古英语 hwær（何处，hwa- 词干）→ 中古英语 where；同族有 whence、wherever、whereabouts。

sensesIntro.en: The word asks for a place, then links clauses to a place, then describes a named place, and finally points at an aspect of an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先询问地点，再把从句系到地点上，随后描述已点明的地点，最后指向论证中的某个方面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip pressed on one spot of a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖压在地图的某一点上。

branches.en: The question branch: where is the key.
branches.cn: 提问分支：钥匙在哪儿。

branches.en: The clause branch: where the children cannot reach.
branches.cn: 从句分支：孩子够不到的地方。

branches.en: The relative branch: the village where she grew up.
branches.cn: 关系分支：她长大的村子。

branches.en: The abstract branch: where the cost is concerned.
branches.cn: 抽象分支：在花费方面。

branches.en: The family branch: somewhere, nowhere and anywhere reuse the stem.
branches.cn: 词族分支：somewhere、nowhere、anywhere 复用同一词干。

intro.en: Where is a free Germanic stem, and its family is built with ever, about and with the combining words some, any and no.
intro.cn: where 是自由的日耳曼语词干，其词族用 ever、about 以及 some、any、no 等构词成分扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin asked the place with ubi and quo, short particles rather than compounds; the entries below are the borrowed parallels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 ubi 与 quo 这类短小虚词询问地点，而非复合词；下面条目是并行说法。

items.example: It works as adverb, conjunction and relative word.
items.exampleCN: 它可作副词、连词和关系词。

items.example: It began as where plus so.
items.exampleCN: 它本是 where 加 so。

items.meaning: in the cases that allow it
items.example: It carries the word into abstract ground.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词带入抽象地带。

definition_zh: 口袋；衣袋；一小块地区；袖珍的；把…据为己有
definition_en: a small bag sewn into clothing for carrying things; a small area or group separated from its surroundings; a smaller than usual version of something; and to take money for oneself, often dishonestly
core_image: 外套内侧缝着一只小布袋，手一探就摸到几枚硬币
scene: 外套挂在门后，手伸进内侧的布兜，摸到几枚温热的硬币。 He slid the coins back into his coat pocket and shut the door.
sceneCN: 这里 pocket 是「口袋、衣袋」（第 1 个义项：缝在衣服上、开口朝上的小布袋）；句意为他把硬币塞回外套口袋，关上了门。图中可辨识物件：门后的外套、内侧布兜、硬币。

collocations.zh: 在某人的口袋里；受某人控制

derivatives.zh: 由 pocket 加表示「一…之量」的后缀 -ful 构成，义为「一袋之量」
由 pocket 与 book 复合而成，义为「钱包；袖珍手册」
由 pocket 与 knife 复合而成，义为「随身小折刀」

senses.title: A small bag sewn into clothing
senses.definition: a small bag or piece of cloth sewn into clothing, open at the top, used for carrying small objects
senses.definitionCN: 缝在衣服上、上端开口、用来装小物件的小布袋或布片
senses.example: He kept the key in his trouser pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钥匙放在裤子口袋里。
senses.why: The word began as a name for any small bag, and when such a bag was stitched inside a garment it stopped being carried and became part of what you wear.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初泛指小袋子；当这种小袋子被缝进衣服里面，它就不再被提在手上，而成了穿着之物的一部分。

senses.title: A small area or group set apart
senses.definition: a small area that differs from what surrounds it, or a small separate group of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 与周围环境不同的一小块地方，或与外界分开的一小群人、一小批事物
senses.example: A pocket of resistance held out in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山间还有一小股抵抗力量在坚持。
senses.why: A pocket holds things apart from the open space around them, and the same containment is pictured on a map: a small patch or group enclosed by something larger.
senses.whyCN: 口袋把东西与周围的空间隔开，同样的「围住」被搬到了地图上：被更大范围包住的一小块地方或一小群人。

senses.title: Small enough to carry in a pocket
senses.definition: small enough to be carried in a pocket, or made in a smaller size than the usual one
senses.definitionCN: 小得可以装进口袋，或做得比通常尺寸更小的
senses.example: She carried a pocket dictionary to class.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着一本袖珍词典去上课。
senses.why: Once a pocket sets the measure of what can be carried on the body, anything built to that measure earns the word as an adjective: a pocket edition fits where a full one cannot.
senses.whyCN: 口袋一旦成为「能随身带走」的尺度，任何按这个尺度做出来的东西就获得了这个形容词：袖珍版放得进大版本放不进的地方。

senses.title: To take money for oneself
senses.definition: to take or keep money that belongs to another person, especially in a quiet or dishonest way
senses.definitionCN: 把属于别人的钱拿走或留下，尤指悄悄地、不诚实地做
senses.example: The clerk pocketed part of the takings.
senses.exampleCN: 那名职员把一部分营业收入装进了自己腰包。
senses.why: To put something in your pocket is to make it disappear from view and keep it, so the physical act becomes a metaphor for quietly keeping money that was never yours.
senses.whyCN: 把东西放进自己口袋，就是让它从眼前消失并留下，于是这个身体动作变成了暗地里留下不属于自己的钱的比喻。

intro.en: Pocket came into English from Anglo-Norman French for a small bag; the older source of that bag word is usually traced to Germanic, though the exact form is uncertain.
intro.cn: pocket 从盎格鲁-诺曼法语中表示小袋的词进入英语；这个小袋词更早的来源一般认为属日耳曼语族，但确切形式不确定。

items.en: A Germanic word for a bag or pouch is usually thought to lie behind the French forms, but no single source form can be reconstructed with confidence.
items.cn: 一般认为法语中的这些形式背后有一个日耳曼语表示袋子、荷包的词，但无法有把握地重构出唯一源头形式，来源不确定。

items.en: Old French poche named a bag or pouch, a soft container gathered at the top rather than a stiff box.
items.cn: 古法语 poche 指袋子、荷包，是一种上端收拢的软容器，而不是硬邦邦的盒子。

items.en: Anglo-Norman added the diminutive ending -et, so poket named a little bag, the size of a handful.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼语加上指小词尾 -et，于是 poket 指一只小袋子，大小不过一把。

items.en: Middle English pocket first meant a small pouch and then the pouch sewn into a garment, which is the sense that fixed the word in everyday use.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pocket 先指小袋，后指缝在衣服上的那只袋子，正是这个义项把词固定在了日常用语里。

items.en: Modern English extends the enclosed space to pockets of resistance and pockets of woodland, uses pocket as an adjective for small sizes, and as a verb for quietly keeping money.
items.cn: 现代英语把这种围起来的小空间扩展到一小股抵抗力量、一小片林地，并用 pocket 作形容词表示小尺寸，作动词表示悄悄把钱留下。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same bag stem and two that only echo its shape; the near-meaning group gathers containers and small enclosures.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个「袋子」词干上的词，另收两个只是形似音近的词；近义组收各类容器与小的封闭空间。

entries.definition: As much as a pocket can hold, formed with the suffix -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 一袋之量；由 pocket 加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: A wallet or a small notebook, a compound whose first element is pocket.
entries.definitionCN: 钱包或袖珍笔记本；由 pocket 与 book 复合而成。

entries.definition: A small parcel or container; it shares the diminutive ending -et but is built on pack, so the two are close in form only.
entries.definitionCN: 小包、小盒；共享指小词尾 -et，却建立在 pack 之上，只是形式相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A figure moved by strings or by a hand; the similarity is in sound and spelling, and the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 用线或手操纵的人偶；只是读音与拼写相近，来源无关。

entries.definition: A small soft bag, often worn at the waist or forming part of an animal's body.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软的小袋子，常系在腰间，或为动物身体的一部分。

entries.definition: A container of soft material with an opening at the top, used for carrying things.
entries.definitionCN: 用软材料制成、上端开口、用来装东西的容器。

entries.definition: A small flat case for carrying money, cards and papers.
entries.definitionCN: 装钱、卡片与票据的小扁盒。

entries.definition: One of the separate sections into which a space is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 把一处空间分隔开来的其中一格。

normalIntro.en: A French word for a small bag sits at the centre, and the family keeps the picture of something enclosed, held close, and kept out of sight.
normalIntro.cn: 核心是一个法语中表示小袋的词，整族词都保留着「被围住、贴身收着、不让人看见」的画面。

normal.en: Old French poche was a bag, and the ending -et made it a little bag, which is exactly what a pocket is.
normal.cn: 古法语 poche 是袋子，词尾 -et 把它变成小袋子，而口袋正是一只小袋子。

normal.en: The oldest English sense is a pouch carried in the hand; only later was it sewn into clothing and worn.
normal.cn: 英语里最古老的义项是提在手上的小袋，后来它才被缝进衣服穿在身上。

normal.en: Pocket money and pocket-sized both use the same measure: what fits in a pocket, or what is small enough to be spent from one.
normal.cn: pocket money 与 pocket-sized 用的是同一个尺度：装得进口袋，或小得能从口袋里掏出来。

normal.en: Pickpocket names the person and the act together, because the thief reaches for the pocket rather than the bag.
normal.cn: pickpocket 把人跟动作合在一起，因为下手的地方是口袋，不是提包。

normal.en: The verb is regular, and to pocket money is simply to make it vanish into that enclosed space.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则；to pocket money 就是让钱消失进那个围起来的地方。

abstract.en: A pocket is a room in a garment: small, private, and closed to everyone else.
abstract.cn: 口袋是衣服里的一间小屋：狭小、私密，对旁人关着门。

abstract.en: A pocket of resistance is the same shape drawn on a map, a small space held inside a larger one.
abstract.cn: 一小股抵抗力量就是把这个形状画在地图上：被更大范围围住的一小块空间。

abstract.en: To pocket what is not yours is to shrink the world until only your own hand remains in it.
abstract.cn: 把不属于自己的东西据为己有，就是把世界缩小到只剩自己的一只手。

examples.en: He kept the key in his trouser pocket.
examples.cn: 他把钥匙放在裤子口袋里。

examples.en: She carried a pocket dictionary to class.
examples.cn: 她带着一本袖珍词典去上课。

examples.en: The clerk pocketed part of the takings.
examples.cn: 那名职员把一部分营业收入装进了自己腰包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕磕它」——口袋里装的都是怕磕碰的小东西，手总护着；记住 pocket 是口袋。

root: pocket 来自盎格鲁-诺曼法语 poket，是古法语 poche（袋子）加指小词尾 -et 而成的小袋；poche 更早的来源一般认为属日耳曼语族，但确切形式不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small bag held close to the body; the senses run from the sewn-in pocket, to an enclosed patch on a map, to the size that fits inside one, and finally to the act of quietly keeping what goes in.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一只贴身的小袋子；义项从缝进衣服的口袋，走到地图上被围住的一小块，再到装得进去的尺寸，最后落到悄悄留下放进来的东西这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cloth bag stitched inside a coat, a hand closing around warm coins.
core.cn: 核心意象：外套内侧缝着的小布袋，手合拢握住几枚温热的硬币。

branches.en: a hand slipping into a coat pocket
branches.cn: 手伸进外套口袋

branches.en: a coin moving from the till into a sleeve
branches.cn: 硬币从钱箱进了袖子

branches.en: a small stand of trees on a bare hill
branches.cn: 光秃山坡上一小片树林

branches.en: a small band holding out in the hills
branches.cn: 山间坚持的一小股人马

branches.en: a dictionary small enough to fit a coat
branches.cn: 小得能塞进外套的词典

intro.en: The word is a French diminutive of a bag noun, and English builds its compounds and its verb from that same enclosed-space picture.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语中「袋子」一词的指小形式，英语又从这个「围起来的小空间」画面造出复合词与动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it reached English through French from a bag word usually traced to Germanic, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它经法语进入英语，源头一般认为属于日耳曼语族中表示袋子的词，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.meaning: as much as a pocket holds

definition_zh: 教育；培养；训练；向公众普及知识
definition_en: to teach, train or develop someone's knowledge, skill and judgment
core_image: 一个人牵着孩子的手，从黑暗的屋子一步步走到门口，门外的光是孩子自己看见的
scene: 博物馆把库房里的标本搬到走廊，让孩子可以伸手触摸并提问。 The museum uses its corridor exhibits to educate visitors about local wildlife.
sceneCN: 这里 educate 指向公众传授知识、培养理解（第 3 个义项：向公众普及）；句意为博物馆用走廊展品向参观者普及本地野生动植物知识。

pos.zh: 教育；培养；训练（可指学校教育，也可指培养判断力）
向公众普及；告知（常与 public、consumers 等搭配）

derivatives.zh: 教育；教育学（由 educate 加表示「动作」的后缀构成，转指培养的过程与制度）
教育工作者（由 educate 加表示「执行者」的后缀构成，转指以教育为职业的人）
教育的；有教育意义的（由 education 加表示「属于」的后缀构成）
有教育作用的（由 educate 加表示「倾向」的后缀构成，转指能带来教益）
引出；使显现（由拉丁 educere「引出」进入英语，与 educate 同源但义不同）

senses.title: To teach in school
senses.definition: to provide formal instruction, usually in a school or college
senses.definitionCN: 通常在学校或学院提供正式教学
senses.example: The school educates children from six to sixteen.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校教育六岁到十六岁的孩子。
senses.why: This is the everyday school sense: an institution and a curriculum carry the act.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的学校义：机构与课程承载这一动作。

senses.title: To bring up and nurture
senses.definition: to care for a person's growth and character over time, not only their knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 长期照料一个人的成长与品格，而不只是知识
senses.example: Her grandmother educated her in patience as much as in letters.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖母教她认字，也教她耐心。
senses.why: The Latin verb began with rearing, and this older sense survives whenever the object is a whole person.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词最初指养育，只要宾语是完整的人，这层古老义就仍在。

senses.title: To inform the public
senses.definition: to help a broad audience understand an issue, often through campaigns, exhibits or media
senses.definitionCN: 通过宣传活动、展览或媒体帮助广泛受众理解某一议题
senses.example: The museum uses its corridor exhibits to educate visitors about local wildlife.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆用走廊展品向参观者普及本地野生动植物知识。
senses.why: The object widens from a pupil to the public, and the verb becomes a form of public communication.
senses.whyCN: 宾语从学生扩到公众，这个动词就变成一种公共传播。

senses.title: To train in a skill
senses.definition: to develop practical ability through instruction and practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过指导与练习发展实际能力
senses.example: The course educates new staff in safe handling of chemicals.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程训练新员工安全处理化学品。
senses.why: Skill training narrows the verb from general development to a demonstrable competence.
senses.whyCN: 技能训练把这个动词从一般发展收窄到可演示的能力。

senses.title: To cultivate taste or judgment
senses.definition: to refine someone's ability to notice, compare and decide
senses.definitionCN: 提升某人察觉、比较与判断的能力
senses.example: Travel educated his eye for architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行培养了他对建筑的眼光。
senses.why: The verb can take an inner faculty as its object, so education becomes the training of perception.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以拿内在能力作宾语，教育于是成为感知的训练。

senses.title: To inform consumers
senses.definition: to give buyers information so that they can choose or use a product responsibly
senses.definitionCN: 向买家提供信息，使其能负责地选择或使用产品
senses.example: The label educates consumers about where the beans were grown.
senses.exampleCN: 标签告知消费者咖啡豆的产地。
senses.why: Business uses the word for disclosure: the seller teaches, though often within a marketing frame.
senses.whyCN: 商业用这个词表示信息披露：卖方在教，尽管常在营销框架内。

senses.title: To educate oneself
senses.definition: to pursue knowledge or skill without being taught by an institution
senses.definitionCN: 不经机构教学而自行追求知识或技能
senses.example: He educated himself in law while working nights.
senses.exampleCN: 他上夜班时自学法律。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the verb inward: the same person is both teacher and learner.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把这个动词转向内部：同一个人既是教师也是学习者。

senses.title: Abstract: to lead out of ignorance
senses.definition: to help someone move from not knowing to knowing, whatever the method
senses.definitionCN: 以任何方式帮助某人从不知走向知
senses.example: A single good question can educate more than a long lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好问题有时比一堂长讲座更能教育人。
senses.why: At its most abstract the verb names the movement of a mind, not a classroom or a syllabus.
senses.whyCN: 推到最抽象处，这个动词命名心智的移动，而非教室或大纲。

intro.en: Educate comes from Latin educare 'to bring up, rear', closely related to educere 'to lead out' (ex- 'out' plus ducere 'to lead'). It entered English in the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: educate 来自拉丁 educare「养育、培养」，与 educere「引出」关系密切，后者由表示「向外」的成分加 ducere「引导」构成。它在十五世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw'. Its family includes conduct, introduce, reduce and produce.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」。其词族包括 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 produce。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ducere gave educere 'to lead out'. The image is drawing a person out of ignorance rather than filling them.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的成分加 ducere 构成 educere「引出」。意象是把人从无知中拉出来，而非往里面填东西。

items.en: Educare meant 'to bring up, rear, nurture'. It is a related verb, and Latin writers already used it alongside educere.
items.cn: educare 意为「养育、抚养、培养」。它是一个相关动词，拉丁作家已把它与 educere 并用。

items.en: English educate appeared in the fifteenth century, first meaning to rear or bring up, then to instruct formally.
items.cn: 英语 educate 在十五世纪出现，最初指养育，后来指正式教导。

items.en: The pair educare and educere are often confused: one stresses nurture, the other the movement out. Both images survive in the English word.
items.cn: educare 与 educere 这对动词常被混淆：一个强调养育，一个强调向外移动。两种意象都留在英语词里。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and relationship): the exact first English use is not recorded, and the precise relation between educare and educere is disputed among etymologists.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与关系）：英语最早用例没有精确记录；educare 与 educere 的确切关系在词源学家之间有争议。

note.en: Group one separates the verb from same-root relatives and from a look-alike of a different root; group two holds the everyday verbs for teaching.
note.cn: 第一组把这个动词与同根亲属词、以及一个异源形近词分开；第二组是表示教导的日常动词。

entries.definition: To draw out something hidden or potential; educate develops a person, while educe extracts what is already there.
entries.definitionCN: 把隐藏或潜在之物引出；educate 发展一个人，educe 则提取已经存在之物。

entries.definition: The process or system; the verb names the act that the noun describes.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或制度；动词命名名词所描述的动作。

entries.definition: From in- 'into' plus ducere: to lead someone into a role or knowledge. It shares the leading root but adds entry.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「进入」的成分加 ducere 构成：把某人引入一个角色或知识。它与「引导」同根，却加上「进入」。

entries.definition: From Latin dicare 'to declare', not ducere. It means to devote or inscribe, with no teaching sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 dicare「宣告」，并非 ducere；意为奉献或题献，没有教学义。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for helping someone learn; educate is more formal and often implies a longer process.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助某人学习的日常动词；educate 更正式，常含较长的过程。

entries.definition: To give explicit directions or lessons; it stresses transmission, while educate can stress development.
entries.definitionCN: 给出明确指令或课程；它强调传递，而 educate 可强调发展。

entries.definition: To develop a specific skill through repeated practice; educate is broader and includes judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 通过反复练习发展特定技能；educate 更宽，包含判断力。

entries.definition: To educate in an institution, or to train someone firmly; it is narrower and often more severe in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 在机构中教育，或严格训练某人；它更窄，语气常更严厉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ducere means lead, so educate is to lead someone out of not knowing.
normal.cn: ducere 意为引导，所以 educate 是把人从不知中引出来。

normal.en: The two Latin verbs split the work: one rears, the other leads out, and English keeps both images.
normal.cn: 两个拉丁动词分工：一个养育，一个引出，英语保留两种意象。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the objects: educate children, educate the public, educate consumers.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示宾语：教育孩子、向公众普及、教育消费者。

normal.en: The reflexive form educates yourself turns the teacher and learner into one person.
normal.cn: 反身形式 educate yourself 把教师与学习者合成一个人。

normal.en: Educe is the bare 'draw out' cousin, with no school attached.
normal.cn: educe 是不带学校的「引出」近亲。

abstract.en: Picture a hand leading a child from a dark room toward a door of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手牵着孩子，从黑屋走向一扇有光的门。

abstract.en: Picture a locked cabinet slowly opened, its contents already inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个上锁的柜子被慢慢打开，里面的东西本来就在。

abstract.en: Picture a question that makes a whole room fall silent and then speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题让整间屋子先静下来，然后开口。

examples.en: The campaign set out to educate voters about the new ballot rules.
examples.cn: 这场运动旨在向选民普及新的投票规则。

examples.en: She was educated at a small school where every class had two teachers.
examples.cn: 她在一所小规模学校受教育，每个班有两名教师。

examples.en: Travel educated his eye for colour long before he studied painting.
examples.cn: 早在他学画之前，旅行就培养了他对颜色的眼光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一丢 凯特」——牵着人往外走，走出无知 → 教育

root: 拉丁 educare「养育、培养」，与 educere「引出」关系密切；educere = 表示「向外」的成分 + ducere「引导」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with school instruction, then move to rearing, public information, skill training, taste, consumer disclosure, self-teaching and finally any movement of a mind out of ignorance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学校教学出发，转到养育、公共普及、技能训练、品味、消费者告知、自学，最后是任何把心智引离无知的移动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand leads a child out of a dark room toward a door of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手牵着孩子，从黑暗的屋子走向一扇有光的门。

branches.en: FORMAL AND PRACTICAL: school instruction, then training in a demonstrable skill.
branches.cn: 正式与实践：先是学校教学，再是可演示的技能训练。

branches.en: GROWTH INSIDE A PERSON: rearing of character, then cultivation of taste and judgment.
branches.cn: 一个人内部的成长：品格的养育，再是品味与判断的培养。

branches.en: OUTWARD INFORMATION: the public is informed, and buyers are told what they need to know.
branches.cn: 向外的信息：公众被告知，买家被告知所需之事。

branches.en: TEACHER AND LEARNER AS ONE: self-education turns the verb inward.
branches.cn: 师生合一：自我教育把这个动词转向内部。

branches.en: THE MOVEMENT ITSELF: the widest reading names a mind leaving ignorance.
branches.cn: 移动本身：最宽的读法命名心智离开无知。

intro.en: Educate is a Latin verb of rearing and leading, and English draws a whole school vocabulary from its two related stems.
intro.cn: educate 是一个表示养育与引导的拉丁动词，英语从它两个相关词干取出一整套学校语汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives conduct and introduce; educare gives educate, education, educator and educative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 conduct 与 introduce；educare 衍生 educate、education、educator 与 educative。

items.example: Educare is the care given on the way.

items.exampleCN: educate 把方向与照料合在一起。

items.structure: educate plus a suffix of action
items.example: The noun names the whole process.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名整个过程。

items.structure: educate plus a suffix meaning 'person who acts'
items.example: The agent ending names the person.

items.structure: educate plus an adjective ending of tendency

items.meaning: to draw out what is hidden
items.example: Educe is the extraction without the school.
items.exampleCN: educe 是不带学校的提取。

definition_zh: 立即；马上；直接地；紧接地
definition_en: at once, without delay, or directly next to something
core_image: 零秒等待：话音未落，行动已开始
scene: 火警铃声突然响起。 The students immediately left the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 immediately 是「立即」（第 1 个义项：毫不拖延地）；句意：学生们立刻离开了教室。

derivatives.zh: 立即的；直接的；形容词基础
即时性；直接性；加名词后缀

senses.title: At once, without delay
senses.definition: without any delay
senses.definitionCN: 毫不拖延地
senses.example: Please call me immediately.
senses.exampleCN: 请立即给我打电话。
senses.why: The gap between event and response shrinks to nothing.
senses.whyCN: 事件与反应之间的间隙缩为零。

senses.title: Directly next to
senses.definition: directly beside or next to, with nothing in between
senses.definitionCN: 紧邻或紧接，中间没有间隔
senses.example: The cottage sits immediately behind the church.
senses.exampleCN: 小屋就在教堂后面紧邻处。
senses.why: The zero gap is spatial: no room lies between two things.
senses.whyCN: 零间隙变成空间的：两物之间没有任何距离。

senses.title: As a conjunction: as soon as
senses.definition: as soon as, in chiefly British use
senses.definitionCN: 主要用于英式英语，意为「一……就」
senses.example: I left immediately the meeting ended.
senses.exampleCN: 会议一结束我就走了。
senses.why: Two events are welded together: the second starts with the first.
senses.whyCN: 两件事被焊在一起：第二件随第一件开始。

senses.title: In the nearest degree of relation
senses.definition: in the closest degree of connection, as with family
senses.definitionCN: 在最紧密的关系层面，如直系亲属
senses.example: Only his immediate family knew the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 只有他的直系亲属知道真相。
senses.why: The zero gap applies to bonds: closest first, no middleman.
senses.whyCN: 零间隙适用于关系：最近者优先，无中间环节。

intro.en: Immediately builds on immediate, from Latin immmediare with the negating prefix in-, to leave nothing in between. The adverb carries both the time sense and the contact sense.
intro.cn: immediately 建立在 immediate 之上，出自拉丁语 immmediare 加否定前缀 in-，意为「中间不留任何东西」。副词兼有时间和接触两义。

items.en: Latin in- plus immediare, to act on something directly, gave immediatus, with nothing intervening.
items.cn: 拉丁语 in- 加 immediare「直接作用于某物」，给出 immediatus「无间隔」。

items.en: The negative prefix in- turned the idea into nothing-in-between.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 把这一概念变成「中间无一物」。

items.en: Late Middle English borrowed immediate in the spatial and relational senses.
items.cn: 中古英语晚期借入 immediate，取空间与关系二义。

items.en: The time sense of immediate and immediately grew strong in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: immediate 与 immediately 的时间义在十七世纪壮大。

items.en: British English added the conjunction use, immediately meaning as soon as.
items.cn: 英式英语加入连词用法，immediately 意为 as soon as。

note.en: The look-alike group lists the immediate family and a near-spelled word. The meaning group compares speed words.
note.cn: 形近组列出 immediate 词族与一个近形词；词义组比较速度类词。

entries.definition: happening at once or with nothing in between.
entries.definitionCN: 立即的；直接的。本词的形容词。

entries.definition: an obsolete spelling seen in early texts.
entries.definitionCN: 早期文本中的旧拼写。

entries.definition: extremely large. It starts the same but comes from a Latin word for measure.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的。开头相同，但源于拉丁语「测量」一词。

entries.definition: at once; emphasizes the instant itself.
entries.definitionCN: 即刻。强调瞬间本身。

entries.definition: at once, in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 马上。口语说法。

entries.definition: immediately; also means simultaneously.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻；也可指同时。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into im + mediate, play on the zero-gap idea and use the conjunction trick.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 im 加 mediate，玩味零间隙概念，并用连词技巧。

normal.en: im + mediately: no middle step is kept between cause and effect.
normal.cn: im 加 mediate：因果之间不留中间步骤。

normal.en: immediately after fixes the position sense: right behind.
normal.cn: immediately after 固定位置义：紧随其后。

normal.en: In British English you can say: I left immediately it ended.
normal.cn: 英式英语可以说：I left immediately it ended。

normal.en: immediate family is the zero-gap circle of relatives.
normal.cn: immediate family 是零间隙的亲属圈。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with immense; one is speed, one is size.
normal.cn: 别和 immense 混淆：一个关于速度，一个关于尺寸。

abstract.en: One image: a hand pressing a button and the light blinking on.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：手按下按钮，灯即刻亮起。

abstract.en: Immediately is time with the waiting taken out.
abstract.cn: immediately 是抽掉等待的时间。

abstract.en: Same zero works in space: no gap between two neighbors.
abstract.cn: 同一个零也用于空间：相邻者之间没有间隙。

examples.en: The doctor came immediately after the call.
examples.cn: 电话一打完医生就来了。

examples.en: He lives immediately opposite the station.
examples.cn: 他就住在车站正对面。

examples.en: Firefighters responded immediately.
examples.cn: 消防员立即出动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一密德里特里」：一秒都不密积等待，德你立刻特里去办。

root: 拉丁语 in-（否定）+ immediare「直接作用」→ immediatus「无间隔」→ immediate「立即的、紧邻的」→ immediately；时间零间隙与空间零间隙同源。

sensesIntro.en: Immediately removes the gap: in time it means at once, in space it means next to, in grammar it welds two events, and in relationships it means closest.
sensesIntro.cn: immediately 消除间隙：时间为「马上」，空间为「紧邻」，语法中焊接两件事，关系上指最亲近。

core.en: Nothing in between: zero gap of time, space, grammar or blood.
core.cn: 中间无一物：时间、空间、语法或血缘上的零间隙。

branches.en: TIME: call me immediately.
branches.cn: 时间：immediately 给我打电话。

branches.en: SPACE: immediately behind the church.
branches.cn: 空间：教堂后紧邻处。

branches.en: SEQUENCE: left immediately it ended.
branches.cn: 先后：一结束就走。

branches.en: RELATION: immediate family.
branches.cn: 关系：直系亲属。

branches.en: POSITION: immediately opposite the station.
branches.cn: 方位：车站正对面。

intro.en: Immediately carries the negative prefix im- over mediate; the family adds immediate, immediacy and mediacy-contrast words.
intro.cn: immediately 在 mediate 上叠加否定前缀 im-；词族加上 immediate、immediacy 及与 mediacy 对照的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the verb of direct action behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的「直接作用」动词。

items.example: The immediate cause was a spark.
The film's immediacy moved the audience.
items.exampleCN: 影片的现场感打动了观众。

items.example: The immediateness of the danger was clear.
The immediately-adjacent lots share a wall.
items.exampleCN: 紧邻的地块共用一堵墙。

definition_zh: 王子；亲王；君主；一方之主；（某领域的）巨子
definition_en: the son of a king or queen, or the male ruler of a small state; also a leading man in a particular activity
core_image: 披着斗篷的年轻人站在王座下一级台阶上
scene: 老国王病重，宫廷内侍捧着王冠站在长廊尽头，等着那位年轻的继承人前来。 The young prince rode through the gate with his guard behind him.
sceneCN: 这里 prince 是「王子」（第 1 个义项：君主之子）；句意为年轻的王子在卫队随行下骑马穿过城门。图中可辨识物件：王冠、长廊、马与卫队。

pos.zh: 王子；亲王；君主；一方之主；巨子

collocations.zh: 童话中的白马王子；理想中的男子
威尔士亲王（英国王位继承人的称号）

derivatives.zh: 由 prince 加 -ly 构成，义为「王子的；如王子般慷慨的」
由 prince 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，义为「公主；王妃」
由拉丁语 princeps 的词干加 -ality 构成，义为「公国；侯国」

senses.title: The son of a monarch
senses.definition: a man or boy who is the son of a king or queen, or a close male member of a royal family
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王之子，或王室中关系亲近的男性成员
senses.example: The prince will take the throne when his mother steps down.
senses.exampleCN: 等母亲退位，这位王子将继承王位。
senses.why: Princeps named the man who took first place in the Roman state, and the title settled on the heir who stands first in line for the crown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 princeps 本指在罗马政权中占第一位的人，这个称号后来落到继承序列里排第一的继承人身上，于是有了「王子」。

senses.title: The ruler of a small state
senses.definition: a royal title held by the male ruler of a principality or by a noble of the highest rank
senses.definitionCN: 授予小国男性统治者或最高等级贵族的王室称号
senses.example: The prince ruled the mountain valley for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位亲王统治那个山谷四十年。
senses.why: Before it meant an heir, the word meant the man who actually held first place in a territory, so it still names the lords of small states.
senses.whyCN: 在指继承人之前，这个词先指真正在一方土地上占据首位的人，所以今天仍用来称呼小国之主。

senses.title: A leading figure in a field
senses.definition: a man who is outstanding in a particular art, trade or profession
senses.definitionCN: 在某一技艺、行业或职业中极为出众的男子
senses.example: He was hailed as the prince of pianists in his day.
senses.exampleCN: 在他那个年代，他被称为钢琴家中的泰斗。
senses.why: If first place can be held in a state, it can also be held in an art, so the title drifted from political rank to personal prestige.
senses.whyCN: 既然首位可以在一个国家里占据，也就能在一门技艺里占据，于是这个称号从政治等级滑向了个人声望。

intro.en: Prince descends from a Latin compound that joins first with take, so the word has always meant the man who occupies the front position.
intro.cn: prince 出自一个把「第一」和「取」合起来的拉丁语复合词，所以这个词一直指占据最前位置的那个人。

items.en: Primus, the Latin adjective for first, supplied the front half of the compound.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 primus 意为「第一」，为这个复合词提供了前半截。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize; in compounds it appears as -ceps, so the whole word pictures taking the first place.
items.cn: capere 意为「取、抓」，在复合词中写作 -ceps，整个词因此描绘出「占取第一位」的画面。

items.en: Princeps named the leading man of the Roman Senate and later the emperor himself.
items.cn: princeps 指罗马元老院中居首位的人，后来也指皇帝本人。

items.en: Old French prince narrowed the title to a ruler of high rank and to the son of a king.
items.cn: 古法语 prince 把这个称号收窄到高级统治者与国王之子。

items.en: English prince covers the monarch's son, the lord of a principality, and by extension a leading man in any field.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prince 既指君主之子、公国君主，也引申指任何领域中的领军人物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the prince family; the near-meaning group gathers titles for rulers and nobles.
note.cn: 形近组收 prince 这一词族；近义组收表示统治者与贵族的称号。

entries.definition: The female counterpart of a prince, by birth or by marriage.
entries.definitionCN: prince 的女性对应称号，因出生或婚姻而获得。

entries.definition: Belonging to a prince, or generous in the manner of one.
entries.definitionCN: 属于王子的；像王子般慷慨的。

entries.definition: A small state ruled by a prince.
entries.definitionCN: 由亲王统治的小国；公国。

entries.definition: First in rank or importance; also the head of a school.
entries.definitionCN: 等级或重要性第一的；也指校长。

entries.definition: A king, queen or other single ruler of a state.
entries.definitionCN: 国王、女王等一国之君。

entries.definition: A person who governs a country or region.
entries.definitionCN: 统治一个国家或地区的人。

entries.definition: A person of high social rank by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 出身高贵的贵族。

entries.definition: A noble of the highest rank below a prince in some systems.
entries.definitionCN: 某些制度中仅次于亲王的最高等级贵族。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Latin adjective for first to the verb for taking, and the whole family keeps that picture of seizing the front place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语「第一」的形容词与「取」的动词拼在一起，整族词都保留着「占取最前位置」的画面。

normal.en: Princeps is primus plus capere: the one who takes the first place, which is why prince means both heir and ruler.
normal.cn: princeps 是 primus 加 capere，即「占取第一位的人」，所以 prince 既指继承人也指统治者。

normal.en: Prime and prince share the same opening, so both point at rank one; only the tail differs, and that tail is about taking.
normal.cn: prime 与 prince 开头相同，都指向第一位；区别只在后半截，而后半截讲的是「取」。

normal.en: Prince Charming is the prince of fairy tales, the man who arrives to close the story.
normal.cn: Prince Charming 是童话里的那位王子，故事靠他出场收尾。

normal.en: A crown prince is the heir standing closest to the throne.
normal.cn: crown prince 是离王位最近的那位继承人。

normal.en: The Prince of Wales is a title for the heir to the British throne, not a separate country.
normal.cn: the Prince of Wales 是英国王位继承人的称号，并不是另一个国家。

abstract.en: A prince is first place made visible: a person standing one step below a throne.
abstract.cn: 王子就是「第一位」的可见形态：一个人站在王座下一级台阶上。

abstract.en: Because the word is built from taking, it carries an edge that birth alone does not: the prince is the one who seizes the front.
abstract.cn: 由于这个词由「取」构成，它带着一种单靠出身得不到的锋利：王子是主动占住最前位置的人。

abstract.en: The same title slides from heir to ruler to master of an art, each of them first in their own circle.
abstract.cn: 同一个称号从继承人滑到统治者，再滑到技艺的宗师，每一个都在自己的圈子里排第一。

examples.en: The prince greeted the villagers from the steps of the palace.
examples.cn: 王子在宫殿台阶上向村民致意。

examples.en: The prince of that region signed a treaty with the neighbouring king.
examples.cn: 那一地区的亲王与邻国国王签订了条约。

examples.en: He was the prince of storytellers in that small town.
examples.cn: 在那座小镇上，他是说故事的人里的头一号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普林斯」——英文姓氏 Prince 音译作「普林斯」，记住这个词本来就是王子、亲王。

root: 拉丁语 princeps 由 primus（第一）加 capere（取）构成，经古法语 prince 进入英语；与 prime 同出 primus，但 prince 多出的 -ceps 表示「取」，所以本义是「占第一位的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the one who takes first place; the senses then spread from the heir of a crown to the ruler of a small state and to a leading man in any field.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「占第一位的人」；义项由此从王位继承人，分到小国之主，再到任何领域中的领军者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young man in a cloak standing one step below a throne.
core.cn: 核心意象：披斗篷的年轻人站在王座下一级台阶上。

branches.en: a young heir standing one step below the throne
branches.cn: 年轻的继承人站在王座下一级

branches.en: a crowd bowing as the heir rides through the gate
branches.cn: 继承人骑马穿门而过，人群躬身

branches.en: a mountain valley governed from a single castle
branches.cn: 一座城堡治理着整个山谷

branches.en: a title held by the lord of a small state
branches.cn: 一位小国之主持有的称号

branches.en: a pianist praised as first among his peers
branches.cn: 被赞为同辈第一的钢琴家

intro.en: The word is a Latin compound of first and take, shortened in French, and later fitted with English endings for the quality, the female form and the territory.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「第一」与「取」的复合词，在法语里缩短，后来再加上英语词尾，分别表示性质、女性形态与领地。

latinIntro.en: Latin princeps is built from primus, first, and the -ceps shape of capere, to take; the same primus also stands behind prime.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 princeps 由 primus（第一）与 capere（取）的复合形态 -ceps 构成；同一个 primus 也支撑着 prime。

definition_zh: 取消；撤销；抵消
definition_en: to stop a planned event, to withdraw an order or decision, or to balance out an effect
core_image: 一支笔在日程表的一行上划掉一道斜线
scene: 下雨了，他们只好取消下午的球赛。 Because of the rain they had to cancel the afternoon match.
sceneCN: 这里 cancel 是「取消」（第 1 个义项：停止已安排好的活动）；句意为因为下雨他们只好取消下午的球赛。

derivatives.zh: 由 cancel 加 -ation 构成，义为「取消；撤销」
由 cancel 加 -er 构成，义为「取消者」
由 cancel 加 -able 构成，义为「可取消的」

senses.title: To stop a planned event
senses.definition: to say that a planned event will not happen
senses.definitionCN: 宣布已安排的活动不再举行
senses.example: Because of the rain they had to cancel the afternoon match.
senses.exampleCN: 因为下雨他们只好取消下午的球赛。
senses.why: The Latin cancelli were the crossed bars of a fence, and to cancel was to cross out with lattice marks.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cancelli 是交叉的栅栏条，cancel 最初就是用交叉的格子线划掉字迹。

senses.title: To withdraw an order
senses.definition: to withdraw an order, a decision or an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 撤回订单、决定或协议
senses.example: She cancelled the order before it was sent.
senses.exampleCN: 她在发货前撤销了订单。
senses.why: Crossing out a written line ended it, so cancel came to mean ending an official order.
senses.whyCN: 在书面文字上划掉一条就等于终止它，于是 cancel 有了终止正式命令的意思。

senses.title: To balance out an effect
senses.definition: to stop one effect by an equal opposite one
senses.definitionCN: 用相等而相反的作用抵消某种效果
senses.example: The two teams cancelled out each other's strengths.
senses.exampleCN: 两支队伍互相抵消了对方的优势。
senses.why: Two crossed strokes wipe each other out, and that picture became the sense of balancing effects.
senses.whyCN: 两笔交叉的划线互相抹掉，这个画面就成了抵消效果的意思。

intro.en: Cancel comes from Latin cancelli, the crossed bars of a lattice, because crossing out a line looked like a small fence.
intro.cn: cancel 来自拉丁语 cancelli，指交叉的栅栏条，因为在文字上划掉一笔就像画了一道小栅栏。

items.en: Cancelli were the crossed bars that made a lattice or fence.
items.cn: cancelli 是构成格子或栅栏的交叉木条。

items.en: Cancellare meant to draw a lattice over writing, and so to cross it out.
items.cn: cancellare 意为在文字上画格子线，也就是划掉。

items.en: Old French cancellers carried the crossing-out sense into law and writing.
items.cn: 古法语 cancellers 把划掉的意思带进法律与文书。

items.en: English cancel first meant to cross out a document and void it.
items.cn: 英语 cancel 最初指在文件上划线使其作废。

items.en: The word widened to events, orders and opposing effects.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到活动、订单和相互抵消的作用。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second collects ways of ending a plan.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收终止计划的词。

entries.definition: A serious disease of cells.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「癌症」，开头与 cancel 相近。

entries.definition: A stick of wax with a wick.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜡烛」，拼写与 cancel 接近。

entries.definition: A group that governs a town.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「委员会」，读音与 cancel 接近。

entries.definition: To decide that a plan will not happen.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「取消」。

entries.definition: To take back an offer or order.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤回」。

entries.definition: To reverse an action.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤销」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Latin origin, the real derivatives and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的拉丁语来源、真实派生词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Latin cancelli were crossed bars, and crossing out a line still cancels it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 cancelli 是交叉的木条，而在文字上划掉一笔至今仍是取消。

normal.en: Cancel first meant to void a document by drawing lines through it.
normal.cn: cancel 最初指在文件上划线使其作废。

normal.en: An order, a flight and a match can all be cancelled.
normal.cn: 订单、航班和比赛都可以被取消。

normal.en: It often pairs with flight, order, meeting and out.
normal.cn: 它常与 flight、order、meeting、out 搭配。

normal.en: Spell c-a-n-c-e-l; British English doubles the l before -ed.
normal.cn: 拼写是 c-a-n-c-e-l，英式英语在 -ed 前双写 l。

abstract.en: See a pen drawing one slanted line through a date: that line is cancel.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在某个日期上划下一道斜线：那道线就是 cancel。

abstract.en: Draw a second line across the first and the two strokes wipe each other out.
abstract.cn: 在第一道上再划一道，两笔就互相抹掉了。

abstract.en: Keep the crossed date in mind and it will give you the word.
abstract.cn: 记住那个被划掉的日期，它就会把这个词交给你。

examples.en: Because of the rain they had to cancel the afternoon match.
examples.cn: 因为下雨他们只好取消下午的球赛。

examples.en: She cancelled the order before it was sent.
examples.cn: 她在发货前撤销了订单。

examples.en: The two teams cancelled out each other's strengths.
examples.cn: 两支队伍互相抵消了对方的优势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坎瑟」——在日程上划一道斜线：取消

root: cancel 来自拉丁语 cancelli，指交叉排列的栅栏条。由它派生的 cancellare 意为在文字上画格子线，也就是划掉作废。这个词经古法语 canceller 进入英语，最初专指在文件上划线使其失效，后来扩展到取消活动、撤销订单。两笔交叉的划线互相抹掉，又生出「抵消」的意思，如两种力量 cancel out。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of cancel grow from one picture: a line drawn through writing to void it.
sensesIntro.cn: cancel 的三个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：在文字上划一道线使其作废。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen drawing one slanted line through a date
core.cn: 核心意象：一支笔在日程表的一行上划掉一道斜线

branches.en: THE EVENT: crossing out a date stops the plan.
branches.cn: 活动线：把日期划掉就停止了计划。

branches.en: THE ORDER: the same stroke voids a written order.
branches.cn: 命令线：同一道划线让书面命令作废。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: two opposite strokes wipe each other out.
branches.cn: 平衡线：两道相反的划线互相抹掉。

branches.en: THE WRITING: events and orders both die on paper.
branches.cn: 书面线：活动与命令都在纸面上被终止。

branches.en: THE REVERSAL: withdrawing and balancing both undo a force.
branches.cn: 反转线：撤回与抵消都在撤掉一股力量。

intro.en: Cancel is a base verb, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: cancel 是基础动词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cancelli, lattice bars, and cancellare, to cross out, are the recorded forms behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cancelli（格子栅栏）与 cancellare（划掉）是这个词背后的有记录形式。

definition_zh: 音乐的；悦耳的；有音乐天赋的；音乐剧
definition_en: connected with music, pleasant to hear like music, gifted at music, and also a stage show built from songs and dialogue
core_image: 舞台幕布升起，歌声与对白在同一束灯光里交替
scene: 排练厅的灯亮到深夜，演员们把同一段合唱重复了一遍又一遍。 The cast rehearsed the new musical until the lights went out.
sceneCN: 这里是「音乐剧」（第 3 个义项：歌曲与对白交替推进的舞台作品）；句意为演员们排练这部新音乐剧，直到灯都灭了。

pos.zh: 音乐的；悦耳的；有音乐天赋的

collocations.zh: 音乐剧剧场；音乐剧艺术

derivatives.zh: 由 musical 加 -ly 构成，义为「在音乐上；悦耳地」
由 musical 加 -ity 构成，义为「音乐性；音乐感」
由 music 加 -ian 构成，指「音乐家」，与 musical 同出 music，并非由 musical 派生

senses.title: Connected with music as an art
senses.definition: belonging to music, or used in the making and study of music
senses.definitionCN: 属于音乐的，或用于创作与研究音乐的
senses.example: She has a musical ear and can pick out a tune after one hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一双音乐的耳朵，听一遍就能把曲调挑出来。
senses.why: The Latin suffix -alis turned musica into musicalis, meaning 'belonging to music', so this sense is the plain label the suffix was made for.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -alis 把 musica 变成 musicalis，意思就是「属于音乐的」，所以这个义项正是该后缀的本职。

senses.title: Pleasant to hear, as if sung
senses.definition: sounding sweet and rhythmical, the way a well-made melody sounds
senses.definitionCN: 听起来甜美而有节奏，像一段做得好的旋律
senses.example: Their voices blended into a musical murmur.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的嗓音融成一片悦耳的低语。
senses.why: A sound orderly enough to resemble music earns the same adjective, so the word moves from 'belonging to music' to 'sounding like music' and becomes praise.
senses.whyCN: 一种声音只要有序到近似音乐，就能用同一个形容词，于是词义从「属于音乐」滑到「像音乐一样好听」，变成一句称赞。

senses.title: A stage or screen work of songs and dialogue
senses.definition: a play or film in which songs and spoken scenes alternate, usually with dancing
senses.definitionCN: 歌曲与说白交替出现、通常还带舞蹈的舞台剧或影片
senses.example: The cast rehearsed the new musical until the lights went out.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们排练这部新音乐剧，直到灯都灭了。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century playbills shortened musical comedy to musical, and the adjective became a noun for an entire kind of show.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的戏单把 musical comedy 缩成 musical，这个形容词于是名词化，指一整类舞台作品。

senses.title: Gifted at music or sensitive to it
senses.definition: naturally aware of pitch and rhythm, or able to play and sing well
senses.definitionCN: 天生对音高与节奏敏感，或演奏演唱得好
senses.example: Even as a child he was unusually musical.
senses.exampleCN: 他小时候就显露出不寻常的音乐天赋。
senses.why: A person whose ear is tuned to music is described by the same adjective, so the word shifts from the art itself to the gift in the person.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵对音乐敏感的人也用这个形容词来描述，于是词义从艺术本身转到人身上的天赋。

intro.en: Musical is the adjective built on Latin musica with the suffix -alis; its noun use for a stage show came much later, from the theatre.
intro.cn: musical 是用后缀 -alis 加在拉丁语 musica 上构成的形容词；指舞台作品的名词用法要晚得多，来自剧院。

items.en: The Greek adjective mousikos described anything of the Muses, including a person trained in song and dance.
items.cn: 希腊语形容词 mousikos 形容一切属于缪斯的东西，也包括受过歌唱与舞蹈训练的人。

items.en: Latin kept musica for the art itself, the noun from which a whole set of adjectives could be built.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 musica 指这门艺术本身，这个名词后来又长出一整组形容词。

items.en: Musicalis added -alis to musica and meant simply 'relating to music', with no hint yet of the stage.
items.cn: musicalis 在 musica 后加 -alis，意思只是「与音乐有关的」，当时还没有舞台的含义。

items.en: Middle French passed musical to English, where it first described anything of music, from voices to instruments.
items.cn: 中古法语把 musical 传给英语，英语最初用它形容一切与音乐有关的东西，从嗓音到乐器。

items.en: In the nineteenth century musical was clipped from musical comedy and became a noun for a show of songs and spoken scenes.
items.cn: 十九世纪，musical 由 musical comedy 缩略而来，变成指「歌曲与说白并存的舞台作品」的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjective's own family and adverbs; the near-meaning group collects words for sounds that please the ear.
note.cn: 形近组收这个形容词的同族形式与副词；近义组收形容声音悦耳的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective is built on, naming the art of sound.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词所依附的名词，指声音的艺术。

entries.definition: The person noun from the same base, formed with -ian rather than -al.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的指人名词，用 -ian 而非 -al 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb built on musical with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musical 后加 -ly 构成的副词。

entries.definition: The noun built on musical with -ity, naming the quality of being musical.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musical 后加 -ity 构成的名词，指音乐性。

entries.definition: Relating to melody, or pleasant because of its melody.
entries.definitionCN: 与旋律有关的；因旋律而动听的。

entries.definition: Having a pleasant tune that is easy to hear and follow.
entries.definitionCN: 曲调优美、容易听清的。

entries.definition: Sweet-sounding, like a well-sung melody.
entries.definitionCN: 音调甜美的，像唱得好的旋律。

normalIntro.en: The adjective sits between the noun music and the person musician, and its suffixes show which one you mean.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词夹在名词 music 与指人的 musician 之间，后缀决定你指的是哪一边。

normal.en: The suffix -al turns the noun music into the adjective musical, just as nation becomes national.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 把名词 music 变成形容词 musical，就像 nation 变成 national 一样。

normal.en: The -al ending marks a quality, while -ian marks a person, which is the clean line between musical and musician.
normal.cn: -al 结尾标记性质，-ian 结尾标记人物，这就是 musical 与 musician 之间清楚的分界。

normal.en: The noun musical began as a short form of musical comedy on nineteenth-century playbills.
normal.cn: 名词 musical 起初是十九世纪戏单上 musical comedy 的缩略形式。

normal.en: A musical instrument is any instrument used for music, a fixed phrase that pins the adjective to its first sense.
normal.cn: a musical instrument 指任何用于音乐的乐器，这个固定搭配把形容词钉在第一个义项上。

normal.en: Musicality is musical plus -ity: the quality of having a musical ear, named as a noun.
normal.cn: musicality 是 musical 加 -ity，把「有音乐耳朵」这种性质变成名词。

abstract.en: One adjective describing a sound, a show and a person's ear shows how a single idea spreads over three very different things.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词既能形容声音、又能形容演出、还能形容人的耳朵，说明一个想法可以铺开到三种很不同的事物上。

abstract.en: When applause follows a song, the adjective quietly turns into a noun without changing a single letter.
abstract.cn: 歌声之后掌声响起，这个形容词便悄悄变成名词，一个字母都没改。

abstract.en: Calling a voice musical is a compliment that measures a human sound against an art form.
abstract.cn: 说一副嗓音 musical，是拿人的声音去比照一门艺术，本身就是称赞。

examples.en: The musical instruments were stored in a padded case.
examples.cn: 乐器被存放在一个带衬垫的箱子里。

examples.en: Her speaking voice is low and musical.
examples.cn: 她说话的声音低沉而悦耳。

examples.en: Tickets for the new musical sold out within a week.
examples.cn: 这部新音乐剧的门票一周内售罄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪齐扣」：缪斯一开口，歌声就扣住人；记住 musical 是音乐的、音乐剧。

root: 一般认为来自晚期拉丁语 musicalis（由 musica 加 -alis 构成），经中古法语 musical 进入英语；名词「音乐剧」是 musical comedy 的缩略。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts as a plain label for anything of music; it then stretches to sounds that please the ear, to a person's ear for music, and finally becomes a noun for a stage show.
sensesIntro.cn: 形容词最初只是「与音乐有关」的标签；随后扩展到悦耳的声音、人的音乐耳朵，最后名词化为一种舞台作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stage curtain rising on a song that carries the story forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台幕布升起，一首歌把故事往前推。

branches.en: a rehearsal room with a piano and a metronome
branches.cn: 摆着钢琴与节拍器的排练房

branches.en: a voice so smooth that the room goes quiet
branches.cn: 嗓音顺滑到让整个房间安静下来

branches.en: a child picking out a tune by ear
branches.cn: 孩子凭耳朵挑出一段曲调

branches.en: a curtain rising on dancers and singers
branches.cn: 幕布升起，舞者与歌者同台

branches.en: an audition settled by the quality of a voice
branches.cn: 由嗓音好坏决定结果的试演

intro.en: The adjective is music plus -al, and two further suffixes, -ly and -ity, turn it into an adverb and a quality noun.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是 music 加 -al，再加 -ly 与 -ity 两个后缀，就得到副词和表示性质的名词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin musicalis is the direct model: musica plus -alis, meaning simply belonging to music.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 musicalis 是直接的样板：musica 加 -alis，意思就是「属于音乐的」。

latinEntries.meaning: of music, and also a musician

definition_zh: 问题；提问；试题；议题；疑问；质疑
definition_en: a sentence that asks for information; a problem set in a test; a matter that needs discussion; doubt about something; to ask someone about something, often with doubt
core_image: 一张被反复折叠的纸，边上写着一个大大的问号
scene: 律师把文件推到桌子中间，指着其中一行，向证人提出一个必须当场回答的问题。 The lawyer asked a question that made the whole room go silent.
sceneCN: 这里 question 是「提问、问题」（第 1 个义项：向别人索取信息的问句）；句意为律师提出的那个问题让整个房间安静下来。画面里可留意：文件、指着一行字的手指、沉默的旁听者。

pos.zh: 问题；提问；试题；议题；疑问

derivatives.zh: question 加 -able，指可疑的、未必可靠的
question 加 -ing，指带着疑问的、追问的
与 question 同族，指一份列出问题供人填写的调查表
un- 加 questionable，指无可质疑的

senses.title: A sentence that asks for information
senses.definition: a sentence or phrase used to ask for information or an answer
senses.definitionCN: 用来索取信息或要求回答的句子或短语
senses.example: She asked a question about the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 她就日程安排提了一个问题。
senses.why: Latin quaestio named the act of seeking, and the English word first names the words used when someone seeks an answer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quaestio 指「寻求」这一行为，英语这个词首先指人们寻求答案时说出的那些话。

senses.title: A problem in a test
senses.definition: a problem or task set in an examination to be answered
senses.definitionCN: 考试中设置出来、需要作答的题目
senses.example: The last question was harder than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一道题比其余的更难。
senses.why: An examination asks many things of the student, so each item on the paper is also one of those asks.
senses.whyCN: 考试向学生提出许多「问」，于是试卷上的每一道题也是一次这样的「问」。

senses.title: A matter that needs settling
senses.definition: a subject or matter that people must discuss and decide
senses.definitionCN: 人们必须讨论并作出决定的事项
senses.example: The question of funding is still open.
senses.exampleCN: 经费问题仍然悬而未决。
senses.why: A matter under discussion is treated as a thing put before the group to be answered, so it too is called a question.
senses.whyCN: 被讨论的事项被当作摆在众人面前、等待回答的东西，所以它也被称作 question。

senses.title: Doubt about something
senses.definition: a feeling of uncertainty about whether something is true or right
senses.definitionCN: 对某事是否真实或正确感到不确定
senses.example: There is no question about her honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 她的诚实是毫无疑问的。
senses.why: If a matter is still open to being asked about, then certainty is missing, and the word comes to name that missing certainty.
senses.whyCN: 一件事如果仍可被追问，就说明确定感缺席，于是这个词转而指这种缺席的确定感。

senses.title: To ask someone about something
