senses.definition: to ask a person about something, especially when you doubt the answer
senses.definitionCN: 向某人询问某事，尤其在怀疑其说法时
senses.example: The police questioned him for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 警察盘问了他一个小时。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into action: putting questions to a person, often to test whether their account holds.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词化为动作：向某人连续发问，常常是为了检验其说法是否站得住。

intro.en: Question comes from the Latin noun for a seeking or inquiry, built on the verb to seek, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: question 源自拉丁语表示「寻求、探究」的名词，由动词「寻求」构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, to search for, and it stands behind a large family of words about asking and investigating.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、寻找，它支撑着一大批关于询问与调查的词。

items.en: Quaestio named the act of seeking and, in law and debate, the matter put forward for an answer.
items.cn: quaestio 指寻求的行为，在法律与辩论中指提出来等待回答的事项。

items.en: Old French question kept both the act of asking and the subject under dispute.
items.cn: 古法语 question 同时保留了「发问」这一行为与「争议中的事项」这两层意思。

items.en: Middle English used the word for an utterance that asks, for a test item and for a doubtful matter.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指发问的话语、试题以及可疑的事项。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb to question, meaning to interrogate or to cast doubt on a claim.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了动词用法，意为审问或对某项主张表示怀疑。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of seeking; the near-meaning group gathers words for inquiries, doubts and disputed matters.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「寻求」词干上的词；近义组收表示询问、怀疑与争议事项的词。

entries.definition: Open to doubt or suspicion.
entries.definitionCN: 可怀疑的；有问题的。

entries.definition: A written set of questions used to collect information.
entries.definitionCN: 用于收集信息的一套书面问题。

entries.definition: A long search for something important.
entries.definitionCN: 为重要目标进行的长期寻找。

entries.definition: A question, especially one raising a doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 问题，尤指提出疑问的问题。

entries.definition: The act of asking for information.
entries.definitionCN: 询问、打听信息的行为。

entries.definition: A subject that people are discussing or arguing about.
entries.definitionCN: 人们正在讨论或争论的话题。

entries.definition: A feeling that something may not be true.
entries.definitionCN: 觉得某事可能不真实的感觉。

entries.definition: A difficulty that needs to be solved.
entries.definitionCN: 需要解决的困难。

normalIntro.en: The word started as the act of seeking an answer and grew into the sentence, the test item, the disputed matter and the doubt itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「寻求答案」这一行为出发，长成问句、试题、争议事项，最后连怀疑本身也叫这个名字。

normal.en: Question and quest share the Latin verb to seek: a question is a small search for an answer.
normal.cn: question 与 quest 共用拉丁语动词「寻求」：一个问题就是一次寻找答案的小旅程。

normal.en: A question mark is literally the written sign of a question, and it turns a statement into an ask.
normal.cn: 问号字面上就是问题的书写符号，它把陈述变成发问。

normal.en: Out of the question means not even worth discussing, as if the matter has been closed before any answer.
normal.cn: out of the question 意为连讨论都不必，好像在得到回答之前事情已经关闭。

normal.en: Questionable means able to be questioned, so a questionable claim is one that invites doubt.
normal.cn: questionable 意为「可被追问的」，所以可疑的说法就是招来怀疑的说法。

normal.en: To question a person is to put a series of questions to them, often to test their story.
normal.cn: to question 一个人就是向他连续发问，常常是为了检验他的说法。

abstract.en: A good question does not merely ask for an answer; it redraws the space in which an answer can be found.
abstract.cn: 好问题不只索取答案，它还重新划出答案可以被找到的那片空间。

abstract.en: Every test item assumes there is one right answer, while a real question often has several.
abstract.cn: 每道试题都假定只有一个正确答案，而真正的问题常常有好几个。

abstract.en: Doubt and inquiry share one word because asking and not knowing are two sides of the same act.
abstract.cn: 怀疑与询问共用一个词，因为发问与不知道本就是同一动作的两面。

examples.en: May I ask a question before we begin?
examples.cn: 开始之前我可以问一个问题吗？

examples.en: Question three on the paper asked for a short explanation.
examples.cn: 试卷第三题要求作简要说明。

examples.en: Nobody questioned the figures, though several people looked uneasy.
examples.cn: 没有人质疑那些数字，尽管有几个人显得不安。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快试称」——遇到问题先快试着称一称分量，再回答，记住 question 是问题、提问。

root: 拉丁语 quaerere（寻求）→ quaestio（探究、问题）→ 古法语 question → 英语 question；同族有 quest、query、questionnaire。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a search for an answer; the senses split into the spoken ask, the test item, the matter to be settled, the doubt and the act of interrogating.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「寻求答案」；义项分为口头发问、试题、待解决的事项、怀疑，以及审问这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a much-folded sheet of paper with a large question mark in the margin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被反复折叠的纸，页边画着一个大大的问号。

branches.en: a hand raised in a classroom
branches.cn: 教室里举起的一只手

branches.en: a numbered line on an exam paper
branches.cn: 试卷上一道编号的题目

branches.en: a folder marked pending on a desk
branches.cn: 桌上标着「待定」的文件夹

branches.en: a pause before an answer
branches.cn: 回答之前的那一顿

branches.en: a lamp left on in an interview room
branches.cn: 审讯室里亮着的一盏灯

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin verb to seek, its noun of action, the French form and English endings that name doubt and repetition.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语动词「寻求」、由它构成的动作名词、法语形式，以及表示怀疑与反复的英语词尾支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around quaerere is wide, and a few of its members are still in English.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 quaerere 的拉丁词群很宽，其中几个成员仍留在英语里。

items.meaning: a doubt put as a question

definition_zh: 海外的；国外的；在海外；向海外；（总称）海外地区
definition_en: located, happening, or living across the sea in a foreign country; also the foreign countries taken together as a region
core_image: 站在海岸线上，越过一条水带望向另一块陆地
scene: 港口堆场里，贴着外文标签的集装箱被吊上货轮。 The shipping clerk wrote overseas on the destination line, and the crane lifted the last box toward the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 overseas 是「海外的、国外的」（第 1 个义项：位于国外）；句意：报关员在目的地一栏写下“海外”，吊机把最后一个箱子吊向大海。图中可辨识物件：集装箱、外文标签、吊机、货轮、报关单、海平线；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 海外的（较早的变体拼法）
驶往海外的；发往国外的

senses.title: Across the sea: located abroad
senses.definition: located or based in a country across the sea from the speaker's own
senses.definitionCN: 位于说话者本国之外、隔海相望的国家
senses.example: The company has three overseas branches.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司有三家海外分公司。
senses.why: Over- means across or beyond, and sea is the water between the two shores. The reference point is always the speaker's own coast; what matters lies on the far side of the water.
senses.whyCN: over- 是“越过、在那边”，sea 是两岸之间的水。参照点始终是说话者自己这一侧的海岸，重要的事物在水的那一边。

senses.title: Coming from abroad
senses.definition: coming from or belonging to a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 来自外国或属于外国的
senses.example: Overseas visitors filled the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 海外游客挤满了博物馆。
senses.why: Here the direction reverses: the word marks not where the thing sits but where it came from. The sea is still the divider, only now the traffic crosses toward the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这里方向反了过来：词标记的不是事物所在之处，而是它来自何处。海仍是分界，只是人流物流朝说话者这一侧越过来。

senses.title: Abroad: the adverbial direction
senses.definition: to or in a country across the sea
senses.definitionCN: 到海外，或在海外
senses.example: She moved overseas after graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业后她移居海外。
senses.why: English lets the same compound serve as an adverb without adding -ly. The phrase names a path, and the path crosses water, so no separate adverb form was ever needed.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许同一个复合词直接作副词，不必加 -ly。这个短语命名的是一条路径，而路径要越过水，因此从来不需要另造副词形式。

senses.title: The overseas as a named region
senses.definition: the countries beyond the sea, taken together as a region or sphere of activity
senses.definitionCN: 隔海之外的国家，作为一个地区或活动领域的总称
senses.example: Sales in the overseas grew faster than at home.
senses.exampleCN: 海外市场的销售增长快于国内。
senses.why: A locational phrase can be nominalized: the far side stops being a direction and becomes a territory with a name. Business and journalism then speak of the overseas as a single place with its own figures.
senses.whyCN: 方位短语可以名词化：那边不再是方向，而变成一块有名字的地盘。商业与新闻于是把“海外”当作一个有自己的数字的单一地方来谈。

senses.title: Foreign affairs: the official sphere
senses.definition: relating to a country's interests and activities beyond its borders
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一国国境之外的利益与活动
senses.example: The ministry handles overseas affairs.
senses.exampleCN: 该部负责海外事务。
senses.why: Bureaucracy names the foreign sphere as an adjective, and activities there become a department's remit. The word turns geography into an administrative portfolio.
senses.whyCN: 官僚体系用形容词命名对外领域，那边的活动就变成一个部门的职责。这个词把地理变成了一份行政分工。

senses.title: Living abroad: of people
senses.definition: of a person or community, living in a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 指个人或群体侨居外国
senses.example: Overseas Chinese communities kept the festival alive.
senses.exampleCN: 海外华人社群把这个节日保留了下来。
senses.why: For people the compound marks residence rather than origin: the person's daily life has moved to the far shore, even if the passport and the language have not.
senses.whyCN: 用于人时，这个词标记的是“居住地”而不是“来源地”：此人的日常生活已经移到海那边，即使护照与语言没有跟着变。

senses.title: Military deployment beyond the sea
senses.definition: of troops or bases, stationed in a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 指部队或基地驻扎在外国
senses.example: The unit served on overseas deployment for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队在海外部署了一年。
senses.why: Armies inherit the maritime image even when they fly. Overseas still means outside the home territory, and the word keeps military language politely vague about which country is meant.
senses.whyCN: 军队即使坐飞机也继承了这个航海意象。overseas 仍指本国领土之外，同时让军事语言礼貌地含糊，不必点明是哪一个国家。

senses.title: Historical euphemism: the colonies
senses.definition: in British usage, a polite word for the colonies and dominions, especially in the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 英国用法中，对殖民地与自治领的委婉说法，尤见于 20 世纪早期
senses.example: Wartime posters promised work in the overseas dominions.
senses.exampleCN: 战时海报承诺在海外自治领有工作机会。
senses.why: Overseas let speakers avoid the word colony. Distance across water replaced a political relationship that many preferred not to name, which is how a neutral geographic term became an instrument of imperial tact.
senses.whyCN: overseas 让说话者避开“colony”这个词。隔海的距离替代了一段许多人不想点明的政治关系，于是一个中性的地理词变成了帝国辞令里的委婉工具。

intro.en: Overseas is a native English compound of over and sea. The word is transparent, but the deeper origin of sea itself is not certain.
intro.cn: overseas 是 over 与 sea 构成的英语本族复合词。词形透明，但 sea 本身的更早来源并不确定。

items.en: The older form oversea is recorded as an adjective and adverb meaning 'across the sea, on the other side of the sea'.
items.cn: 较早的形式 oversea 记录于 15 世纪，作形容词与副词，意为“隔海、在海的那一边”。

items.en: Overseas appears with the same meaning and eventually displaces oversea in most contexts. Both are simply over + sea.
items.cn: overseas 于 16 世纪 80 年代出现，意义相同，最终在多数语境中取代 oversea。两者都只是 over + sea。

items.en: British imperial usage makes overseas a euphemism for the colonies and dominions, especially during the First World War.
items.cn: 英国帝国用语把 overseas 变成殖民地与自治领的委婉说法，尤在第一次世界大战期间。

items.en: The noun use is recorded: the overseas as the collective name for territories beyond the sea.
items.cn: 名词用法记录于 1919 年：the overseas 作为隔海之外领土的集合名称。

items.en: Trade, education, and the military keep the word busy: overseas market, overseas students, overseas deployment. The geographic frame stays neutral, which is exactly why it survives.
items.cn: 贸易、教育与军事让这个词持续活跃：海外市场、留学生、海外部署。它的地理框架保持中性，这也正是它存活下来的原因。

note.en: The first group collects over- words that look similar but do not mean across the sea. The second compares words for foreignness and distance.
note.cn: 第一组是同样带 over-、外形相近却不表示“隔海”的词。第二组比较表示“异国、远方”的词。

entries.definition: to watch over and supervise work or people. It sounds almost the same but has no sea in it.
entries.definitionCN: 监督、管理工作的进行。读音几乎相同，但里面没有 sea。

entries.definition: larger than the standard size. It shares over- and the -size ending but means excess, not distance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过标准尺寸的。它同样带 over- 和 -size 结尾，但表示“过大”，而不是距离。

entries.definition: to express something more strongly than is justified. Its over- means too much, not across.
entries.definitionCN: 把话说得过头；夸大。它的 over- 表示“过分”，不是“越过”。

entries.definition: a loose garment worn over other clothes. It is over + all, and the plural -s can be mistaken for the -s of overseas.
entries.definitionCN: 穿在其他衣服外面的宽松工装。它是 over + all，复数 -s 容易被误当成 overseas 的 -s。

entries.definition: in or to a foreign country. It is only an adverb, while overseas can also be an adjective and a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在外国、到外国。它只能作副词，而 overseas 还能作形容词和名词。

entries.definition: belonging to a country other than one's own. It is the plain adjective and needs no sea, while overseas keeps the maritime image.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本国以外国家的。它是最朴素的形容词，不需要海；overseas 则保留了航海意象。

entries.definition: involving two or more nations. It stresses relations between states, while overseas stresses distance from home.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及两个或多个国家的。它强调国家之间的关系，overseas 强调与本土的距离。

entries.definition: away from the shore, especially of islands used for financial reasons. It is about distance from land, not about another country.
entries.definitionCN: 离岸的，尤指用于金融目的的海岛。它说的是离开陆地，而不是到另一个国家。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the over + sea picture, then three abstract images about distance and how it is used.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 over + sea 画面的挂钩，再用三个关于距离及其用法的抽象画面。

normal.en: Say it as over-seas: over the seas, not over the sees. The plural seas are the water you cross.
normal.cn: 把它读成 over-seas：越过一片片海，而不是 over the sees。复数 seas 就是你越过的水。

normal.en: Look at a map: your finger starts on the home coast, crosses blue, and lands on another country. That finger path is overseas.
normal.cn: 看地图：手指从本国海岸出发，越过蓝色，落到另一个国家。那条手指路径就是 overseas。

normal.en: overseas students are students who crossed the sea to study; the sea is in the name, not in their luggage.
normal.cn: overseas students 是越过海来读书的学生；海在名字里，不在他们的行李里。

normal.en: The word has no -ly adverb form because it already works as an adverb: go overseas, live overseas.
normal.cn: 这个词没有 -ly 副词形式，因为它本身就能作副词：go overseas、live overseas。

normal.en: Overseas trade is trade that leaves the harbour; if the goods never touch water, the word still keeps the old picture.
normal.cn: overseas trade 是离开港口的贸易；即使货物从不碰水，这个词仍保留着旧画面。

abstract.en: Overseas is distance turned into a category: the far shore becomes an administrative box.
abstract.cn: overseas 是把距离变成一个分类：远岸被装进一个行政抽屉。

abstract.en: Every overseas is someone's home. The word marks the speaker's shore, not an absolute edge of the world.
abstract.cn: 每一个“海外”都是某些人的家。这个词标记的是说话者的海岸，而不是世界的绝对边缘。

abstract.en: The word is neutral geography doing political work: it can name a colony without saying colony.
abstract.cn: 这个词让中性的地理替政治干活：它可以指殖民地，却不必说出 colony。

examples.en: The firm opened an overseas office in Osaka last spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年春天在大阪开设了海外办事处。

examples.en: Many overseas students work part-time while they improve their English.
examples.cn: 许多留学生在提高英语的同时做兼职。

examples.en: The letters went overseas by ship and took six weeks to arrive.
examples.cn: 这些信件经海路寄往海外，走了六周才到。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 over 记成“越过”，sea 记成“海”：越过海的那一边，就是海外。
dict_mnemonic.text: over（越过）+ sea（海）+ -s → 海外的、在海外；海外地区

root: over（越过）+ sea（海）；sea 是日耳曼语固有词，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow the direction of travel: first something sits on the far shore, then it comes toward the speaker, then the word becomes a path, a named region, an official portfolio, a way of living, a military station, and finally a polite imperial word for the colonies.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项顺着旅行的方向展开：先有东西位于远岸，再有东西朝说话者这边来，随后这个词变成一条路径、一块被命名的地区、一份官方职责、一种居住方式、一处军事驻地，最后成为帝国辞令里对殖民地的委婉说法。

core.en: A coastline, a band of water, and another land on the far side
core.cn: 一条海岸线、一条水带，以及水那边另一块陆地

branches.en: A place across the sea: the word locates something abroad.
branches.cn: 海那边的地方：这个词指某物位于国外。

branches.en: From a path to a place: the adverb of movement becomes a named region.
branches.cn: 从路径到地方：表示移动的副词变成一块被命名的地区。

branches.en: The official sphere: foreign affairs at a desk, and troops in the field.
branches.cn: 官方领域：办公桌上的对外事务，以及战场上的海外驻军。

branches.en: People: those who live and work across the sea.
branches.cn: 人：在海外生活与工作的那些人。

branches.en: Origin and old tongue: goods that come from across the sea, and the older British label for the colonies.
branches.cn: 来源与旧称：从海那边来的货物，以及英国旧时对殖民地的说法。

intro.en: Overseas is built from the over- prefix and the sea family. The items below include both true relatives and the nearest sea compounds, so the boundary of the family is visible.
intro.cn: overseas 由 over- 前缀和 sea 词族构成。下面既有真正的同族词，也有最接近的海事复合词，以便看清词族的边界。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: over is Old English ofer (PIE *uper), and sea is Old English sæ, from Proto-Germanic *saiwiz, whose deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：over 是古英语 ofer（原始印欧语 *uper），sea 是古英语 sæ，来自原始日耳曼语 *saiwiz，其更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: across the sea; in or from a foreign country
items.meaningCN: 隔海；在海外或来自海外

items.meaning: the earlier adjective and adverb, now mostly replaced
items.meaningCN: 较早的形容词与副词形式，现已多被取代
items.example: An oversea cable was laid in 1866.
items.exampleCN: 一条海底电缆于 1866 年铺设。

items.meaning: the salt water that covers most of the earth
items.meaningCN: 覆盖地球大部分区域的咸水
items.example: The sea was calm that morning.
The seaward window caught the wind.

items.meaning: working or traveling on the sea
items.example: A seafaring family kept the old charts.
items.exampleCN: 一个航海世家保存着旧海图。

items.meaning: away from the shore; of financial islands
items.meaningCN: 离岸的；金融意义上的离岸

items.example: A transoceanic flight takes twelve hours.
items.exampleCN: 跨洋飞行需要十二小时。

definition_zh: 想象；设想；猜想；臆造
definition_en: to form a picture or idea of something in the mind
core_image: 在脑内放映一场不存在的电影
scene: 孩子们的教室里。 Imagine you are sailors on a windy sea.
sceneCN: 这里 imagine 是「想象、设想」（第 1 个义项：在脑中构建图景）；句意：想象你们是狂风大作的海上的水手。

derivatives.zh: 虚构的；假想的；加形容词后缀

senses.title: To picture in the mind
senses.definition: to form a mental image of something not present
senses.definitionCN: 为不在眼前的事物在心中形成图像
senses.example: Close your eyes and imagine the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 闭上眼睛想象那片海滩。
senses.why: The mind projects a scene onto its dark screen.
senses.whyCN: 心灵把一幕场景投射到自己的暗幕上。

senses.title: To suppose or believe
senses.definition: to assume or believe something to be true
senses.definitionCN: 假定或认为某事属实
senses.example: I imagine he forgot the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜他忘了开会。
senses.why: The mental picture hardens into a tentative belief.
senses.whyCN: 心中的图像凝固成初步的判断。

senses.title: To invent something unreal
senses.definition: to create something that does not exist
senses.definitionCN: 创造出不存在的东西
senses.example: The author imagined a city under the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 作者虚构了一座海底之城。
senses.why: The projector is set free: it makes worlds that were never filmed.
senses.whyCN: 放映机被放开：它造出从未被拍摄的世界。

senses.title: To conceive a possibility
senses.definition: to think of something as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把某事设想为可能
senses.example: Imagine winning the prize twice.
senses.exampleCN: 设想两次赢得这个奖。
senses.why: The mind rehearses an outcome before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 心灵在结果发生前先进行彩排。

senses.title: To wrongly believe
senses.definition: to believe wrongly that something is happening
senses.definitionCN: 错误地相信某事正在发生
senses.example: You imagined the footsteps; the street was empty.
senses.exampleCN: 脚步声是你幻听，街上空无一人。
senses.why: The projector runs without light: false pictures feel real.
senses.whyCN: 放映机在无光时运转：虚假的图像也显得真实。

intro.en: Imagine comes from Latin imaginari, to picture to oneself, from imago, an image or copy. French imagine carried it into English, keeping the picture at the heart of the word.
intro.cn: imagine 来自拉丁语 imaginari「在心中成像」，词基 imago「影像、摹本」。法语 imagine 把它带入英语，词心始终是「图像」。

items.en: Latin imago meant a copy, portrait or mental image; the ancestor of English image.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imago 指摹本、肖像或心中影像；是英语 image 的祖先。

items.en: The verb imaginari meant to form such images in the mind.
items.cn: 动词 imaginari 意为在心中形成这类影像。

items.en: Old French imaginer passed the verb to medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 imaginer 把该动词传给中世纪欧洲。

items.en: Middle English imagine at first meant to form a mental picture, then to devise a plan.
items.cn: 中古英语 imagine 先指在心中成像，继而指谋划。

items.en: Modern English built imagination, imaginary and imaginative around it.
items.cn: 现代英语围绕它构建 imagination、imaginary 与 imaginative。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the image family and two confusing neighbors. The meaning group compares thinking verbs.
note.cn: 形近组收录 image 词族与两个易混邻词；词义组比较思考类动词。

entries.definition: the power or act of imagining.
entries.definitionCN: 想象力。本词加后缀的名词。

entries.definition: existing only in the imagination.
entries.definitionCN: 虚构的。只存在于想象中。

entries.definition: showing creativity; describes people and ideas, not unreal things.
entries.definitionCN: 有创意的。形容人与想法，不指虚幻之物。

entries.definition: to visualize, usually more concretely than imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 设想。通常比 imagine 更具体。

entries.definition: to assume without proof, close to sense 02.
entries.definitionCN: 假定。接近第 2 义项。

entries.definition: to imagine while asleep or wistfully awake.
entries.definitionCN: 做梦；遐想。睡中或怅然醒时的想象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split imagine into image + ine, reuse just imagine, and warn about the imaginary-imaginative trap.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 imagine 拆成 image 加 ine，复用 just imagine，并警示 imaginary 与 imaginative 之辨。

normal.en: See image inside imagine: to imagine is to paint an image in your head.
normal.cn: 在 imagine 里看到 image：想象就是脑内作画。

normal.en: just imagine opens a daydream: just imagine living on the moon.
normal.cn: just imagine 开启一段白日梦：就想想住在月球上。

normal.en: I imagine takes guesses: I imagine he is late.
normal.cn: I imagine 承载猜测：我猜他迟到了。

normal.en: imaginary things do not exist; imaginative people create.
normal.cn: imaginary 的东西不存在；imaginative 的人有创造力。

normal.en: Spelling trap: no a before g in imagine, unlike the noun image plus ine.
normal.cn: 拼写陷阱：imagine 中 g 前没有 a，与名词 image 加 ine 不同。

abstract.en: One image: a small cinema behind the eyes.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：眼睛后面的小电影院。

abstract.en: Imagining is practicing reality before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象是现实到来前的彩排。

abstract.en: Careful: the projector sometimes runs without the light of truth.
abstract.cn: 小心：放映机有时在没有真相之光时运转。

examples.en: Imagine living a hundred years from now.
examples.cn: 想象一下生活在百年之后。

examples.en: I imagine the trip will take six hours.
examples.cn: 我猜这趟旅程要六个小时。

examples.en: She imagined a machine that could fly long before one existed.
examples.cn: 早在飞机出现之前她就设想了会飞的机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一摸镜」：伸手一摸镜子，镜中世界全靠想象。

root: 拉丁语 imago「影像」→ imaginari「心中成像」→ 古法语 imaginer → 中古英语 imagine；词义从成像扩展到猜想、虚构与幻听。

sensesIntro.en: Imagine projects pictures, hardens them into guesses, builds unreal worlds, rehearses futures, and sometimes runs falsely.
sensesIntro.cn: imagine 投射图像，把图像凝成猜测，搭建虚幻世界，彩排未来，有时还会虚假运转。

core.en: The mind's projector: images shown before or beyond reality.
core.cn: 心灵的放映机：在现实之前或之外放映影像。

branches.en: PICTURE: imagine the beach at sunset.
branches.cn: 图像：想象日落时分的海滩。

branches.en: SUPPOSITION: I imagine he is late.
branches.cn: 猜想：我猜他迟到了。

branches.en: INVENTION: a city imagined under the sea.
branches.cn: 虚构：设想的 underwater 城市。

branches.en: PROSPECT: imagine winning twice.
branches.cn: 设想：想象两次夺奖。

branches.en: ILLUSION: footsteps you imagined in the empty street.
branches.cn: 幻觉：空街上幻听到的脚步声。

intro.en: Imagine keeps its Latin image at the center; the family adds imagination, imaginary, imaginative and the simpler image.
intro.cn: imagine 的中心始终是拉丁语「影像」；词族加上 imagination、imaginary、imaginative 与更简的 image。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the noun imago and the verb imaginari that fed the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示 imago 名词与 imaginari 动词，整个词族由此而来。

items.example: Imagine a door in this wall.

items.meaning: the power of forming mental images
items.example: Her imagination filled the empty room.
items.exampleCN: 她的想象力填满了空屋。

items.example: The dragon is an imaginary friend.
items.exampleCN: 那条龙是个虚构的朋友。

items.example: An imaginative solution saved the day.
items.exampleCN: 富有想象力的方案扭转了局面。

items.example: The screen showed a sharp image.

items.exampleCN: 想象中的威胁从未到来。

items.example: The book collects her early imaginings.
items.exampleCN: 此书收录了她早期的想象之作。

latinEntries.meaning: to form an image in the mind

definition_zh: 考试；检查；审查；诊察；质证
definition_en: a formal test of knowledge, or a careful inspection of something
core_image: 天平中央那根指针：一边放砝码，一边放待称的东西，指针偏转就说明重量。
scene: 考场上，学生翻开试卷，计时器开始走动；同一周里，医生也在给另一位病人做检查。 In the hall a student opens the paper as the timer starts, and that same week a doctor carries out an examination of another patient.
sceneCN: 这里 examination 同时体现「考试」和「医学检查」两个意思（考场用第 1 个义项，身体检查用第 3 个义项）；句意：考场里学生翻开试卷、计时器开始走动；同一周里，医生也在给另一位病人做检查。

pos.zh: 考试；检查；审查；诊察；（法律）质证；检验

senses.title: A formal test
senses.titleCN: 考试：用题目测知识或能力
senses.definition: a formal test of knowledge or ability, usually written or spoken
senses.definitionCN: 对知识或能力的正式测试，通常为笔试或口试
senses.example: The final examination covers everything from the first term.
senses.exampleCN: 期末考试覆盖第一学期以来的全部内容。
senses.why: A test is a weighing: the candidate's knowledge is placed against a fixed standard, and the mark records the difference.
senses.whyCN: 考试就是一次称重：考生的知识被放到固定标准旁，分数记录了两者的差距。

senses.title: Close inspection
senses.definition: a careful look at something in order to find out its condition or details
senses.definitionCN: 为查明状况或细节而仔细查看某物
senses.example: A close examination showed a hairline crack in the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细检查发现框架上有一条细裂缝。
senses.why: The original image is a balance pointer: examination is the act of bringing something under scrutiny so that its hidden weight shows.
senses.whyCN: 原意象是天平的指针：examination 就是把东西放到审视之下，让隐藏的‘重量’显现。

senses.title: Medical examination
senses.titleCN: 医学检查：把身体放到诊断标准下
senses.definition: a physical or clinical check of a patient's body or health
senses.definitionCN: 对病人身体或健康状况进行的体格或临床检查
senses.example: The doctor began the examination with the patient's breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 医生从病人的呼吸开始检查。
senses.why: The body becomes the object weighed against normal signs; the examination looks for what departs from the expected range.
senses.whyCN: 身体成为对照正常体征被称量的对象；检查寻找的是偏离预期范围的部分。

senses.title: Cross-examination
senses.titleCN: 法律质证：用问题检验证词
senses.definition: the questioning of a witness by the opposing side in a legal case
senses.definitionCN: 法律案件中由对方对证人进行的提问与检验
senses.example: Cross-examination exposed a contradiction in the witness's account.
senses.exampleCN: 交叉质证暴露了证人陈述中的矛盾。
senses.why: A witness's story is put on the scale of other evidence; each question tests whether it still balances.
senses.whyCN: 证人的说法被放到其他证据的天平上；每个问题都在检验它是否仍然平衡。

senses.title: Official inquiry
senses.titleCN: 官方审查：对事件与账目立案调查
senses.definition: a formal investigation by an authority into an event or a set of records
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构对事件或记录进行的正式调查
senses.example: The committee's examination of the accounts lasted six months.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对账目的审查持续了六个月。
senses.why: An authority sets the standard and compels the records to be produced; the examination is the forced comparison.
senses.whyCN: 权威设定标准并强制调取记录；examination 就是这场强制性的对照。

senses.title: Academic scrutiny
senses.titleCN: 学术审查：把论文与证据逐条核对
senses.definition: the critical review of a scholarly claim, text, or body of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 对学术主张、文本或证据体系进行的批判性审查
senses.example: The theory did not survive examination by later researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论没能经受后来研究者的审查。
senses.why: In scholarship the balance is evidence: a claim is examined by asking whether the evidence outweighs the objections.
senses.whyCN: 学术里的天平是证据：审查一个主张，就是问证据是否压过反方意见。

senses.title: Laboratory test
senses.titleCN: 化验：把样本放到仪器里检验
senses.definition: a laboratory procedure that tests a sample for particular substances or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室检验样本中特定物质或状况的程序
senses.example: Examination of the water sample revealed high lead levels.
senses.exampleCN: 对水样的化验显示铅含量偏高。
senses.why: Here the instrument replaces the human eye; the sample is examined because its contents are not visible without a test.
senses.whyCN: 这里仪器替代了眼睛；样本之所以被检验，是因为不测试就看不见其中的成分。

senses.title: Testing a hypothesis
senses.definition: the process of testing a hypothesis, idea, or method against evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用证据对假设、观点或方法进行检验的过程
senses.example: The proposal came under examination during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 该方案在试验期间受到了检验。
senses.why: An idea is examined by putting it in a situation where it could fail. Passing the examination is not proof, only survival so far.
senses.whyCN: 检验一个想法，就是把它放进可能失败的处境。通过检验不是证明，只是截至目前还活着。

intro.en: Examination comes from Latin examen, the tongue or pointer of a balance, and examinare, to weigh or test. The weighing image is older than the school sense.
intro.cn: examination 来自拉丁 examen（天平的指针）与 examinare（称量、检验）。‘称重’的意象比‘考试’义更古老。

items.en: The pointer or tongue of a balance, hence a means of weighing. The word names the instrument that reveals weight, not the weight itself.
items.cn: 天平的指针或舌，因而指称量的手段。这个词命名的是显示重量的器具，而不是重量本身。

items.en: To drive out, to demand, to weigh. Many sources connect examen with exigere, but the link is reconstructed rather than directly attested; it is best marked as generally accepted, not certain.
items.cn: 驱出、索取、称量。许多来源把 examen 与 exigere 联系起来，但这是重构而非直接可证的联系；宜标为“一般认为是”，不是确定结论。

items.en: To weigh, test, or examine. The verb extends the balance image to any careful assessment of a thing's value or truth.
items.cn: 称量、检验、审查。该动词把天平意象扩展到对事物价值或真实性的任何仔细评估。

items.en: Old French passed the noun to English. The French form kept both the legal and the scholarly possibilities of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 古法语把该名词传给英语。法语形式同时保留了拉丁动词的法律与学术两种可能。

items.en: English examination is recorded from the 14th century, first in legal and religious inquiry, then in academic testing.
items.cn: 英语 examination 自 14 世纪有记录，先用于法律与宗教调查，后用于学业测试。

items.en: The school examination became fixed in the 19c as public education expanded. Medicine and science kept the older sense of inspecting a body or a sample.
items.cn: 19 世纪公共教育扩张，学校‘考试’义固定下来；医学与科学则保留更古老的‘检查身体或样本’义。

note.en: The first group is the examine family; the second compares kinds of checking, from a scored test to a broad inquiry.
note.cn: 第一组是 examine 词族；第二组比较各种‘检查’，从计分考试到广泛调查。

entries.definition: to inspect or test something carefully. It is the action behind examination.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细检查或检验；是 examination 背后的动作。

entries.definition: a person who sets or marks an examination, or who inspects something officially.
entries.definitionCN: 出题或评卷的人，或进行官方检查的人。

entries.definition: a person who is being examined, especially in a test. The suffix -ee marks the receiver.
entries.definitionCN: 接受考试或检查的人；后缀 -ee 标记接受者。

entries.definition: the informal short form of examination in the school sense. It is not used for medical inspection.
entries.definitionCN: 学校义项中 examination 的非正式缩略；不用于医学检查。

entries.definition: a procedure that measures ability or quality, often with a score. It is the everyday word for a school examination.
entries.definitionCN: 测量能力或质量的程序，常带分数；是学校考试的日常用词。

entries.definition: an official or careful look at something to check its condition. It stresses seeing rather than questioning.
entries.definitionCN: 为核查状况而进行的官方或仔细查看；强调‘看’，而非‘问’。

entries.definition: a judgement of quality, ability, or risk. It is broader than a single examination.
entries.definitionCN: 对质量、能力或风险的判断；比单次考试更宽泛。

entries.definition: a formal or systematic investigation into a question. It emphasizes seeking facts, not grading.
entries.definitionCN: 对某个问题的正式或系统调查；强调寻找事实，而非评分。

entries.definition: a quick check to identify cases that need closer attention. It is an examination used as a filter.
entries.definitionCN: 为找出需要进一步关注的对象而做的快速检查；是作为筛选器的 examination。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin examen, the pointer of a balance, plus -ation. The word asks what something weighs when placed against a standard.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁 examen‘天平指针’加 -ation。这个词问的是：把某物放到标准旁，它有多重。

normal.en: A balance pointer is the original examination: it shows the hidden weight.
normal.cn: 天平指针就是最初的 examination：它让隐藏的重量显形。

normal.en: An exam paper is a balance: your answer on one side, the mark scheme on the other.
normal.cn: 试卷就是天平：一边你的答案，一边评分标准。

normal.en: A doctor's examination puts your body beside normal ranges.
normal.cn: 医生的 examination 把身体放到正常范围旁边。

normal.en: Cross-examination weighs one story against other evidence.
normal.cn: 交叉质证用其他证据来称量一个说法。

normal.en: A lab examination reveals what the eye cannot weigh.
normal.cn: 实验室检查揭示眼睛称不出来的东西。

abstract.en: To examine is to risk an answer, not to confirm one.
abstract.cn: 审查是让答案承担风险，而不是确认答案。

abstract.en: Every examination chooses its instrument, and the instrument decides what can be found.
abstract.cn: 每次检查都选择自己的仪器，而仪器决定了能发现什么。

abstract.en: A test measures the answer, not the person; the confusion between them is a social fact.
abstract.cn: 考试测量的是答案，不是人；把两者混为一谈是一种社会事实。

examples.en: The examination was moved online after the snow closed the school.
examples.cn: 大雪停课后，考试改到了线上。

examples.en: A second examination of the manuscript found a date written in a later hand.
examples.cn: 对抄本的再次检查发现了一个后来补写的日期。

examples.en: Under examination, the witness admitted he had not seen the car.
examples.cn: 在质证中，证人承认他并没有看见那辆车。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一个贼，没捏住”——考试时想作弊，被老师“捏住”检查：examination 检查、考试。

root: 源自拉丁 examen（天平指针）与 examinare（称量、检验），经古法语 examinacion 进入英语；核心是“把对象放到标准上称一称”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of examination, one gesture: place something against a standard and see how it weighs. The standard can be a mark scheme, a normal range, another witness, an authority's rule, a body of evidence, or an instrument.
sensesIntro.cn: examination 的八个义项共用一个动作：把对象放到标准上，看它有多重。标准可以是评分方案、正常范围、另一份证词、权威规则、证据体系或仪器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the pointer of a balance swinging as a weight is placed on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：砝码放上一边时，天平指针摆动。

branches.en: TESTING CLAIMS: a school paper and a scholarly thesis are both weighed against a standard.
branches.cn: 检验主张：试卷与学术论文都被放到标准上称量。

branches.en: BRINGING TO LIGHT: close inspection and hypothesis testing reveal what was hidden.
branches.cn: 让隐者显形：仔细检查与假设检验都揭示隐藏的东西。

branches.en: READING THE BODY OR SAMPLE: the clinic and the laboratory use instruments to weigh what the eye cannot see.
branches.cn: 读取身体或样本：诊所与实验室用仪器称量眼睛看不见的东西。

branches.en: QUESTIONING A WITNESS: cross-examination weighs one account against other evidence.
branches.cn: 质询证人：交叉质证用一个说法对账其他证据。

branches.en: INVESTIGATING RECORDS: an authority compels documents into the open for comparison.
branches.cn: 调查记录：权威强制把文件摆出来做对照。

intro.en: Examination is examin- plus -ation. English also has the verb examine, the person nouns examiner and examinee, and the clipped form exam.
intro.cn: examination 是 examin- 加 -ation。英语还有动词 examine、人物名词 examiner 与 examinee，以及缩略形式 exam。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are examen, examinare, and exigere. The connection between examen and exigere is generally accepted but reconstructed, so it should not be presented as certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁形式是 examen、examinare、exigere。examen 与 exigere 的联系被普遍接受，但属于重构，不应说成确定事实。

items.example: The panel examined every page of the report.
items.exampleCN: 专家组审查了报告的每一页。

items.example: The examiner checked the seal on each sample.
items.exampleCN: 审查员检查了每个样本上的封条。

items.example: Each examinee received a numbered desk.
items.exampleCN: 每位应试者拿到一张编号课桌。

items.example: She has three exams next week.

items.meaning: to question a witness for the opposing side
items.example: The lawyer cross-examined the witness for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 律师盘问证人一个小时。

items.meaning: the questioning of a witness by the other side
items.example: Cross-examination is limited to the scope of direct testimony.
items.exampleCN: 交叉质证限于直接证词的范围。

items.meaning: precise, or to demand and obtain
items.meaningCN: 精确的；强求；源自 exigere‘驱出、索取’
items.example: The exact wording of the clause matters.
items.exampleCN: 该条款的精确措辞很重要。

items.meaningCN: 紧急的；迫切需要处理的
items.example: The exigent circumstances justified a late-night call.
items.exampleCN: 紧急情况使得深夜致电成为正当。

items.example: The budget was cut in response to a fiscal exigency.
items.exampleCN: 为应对财政紧急状况，预算被削减。

latinEntries.meaning: the tongue or pointer of a balance; a weighing

latinEntries.meaningCN: 驱出；索取；称量（与 examen 的联系属一般认为）

definition_zh: 架子；搁板；暗礁
definition_en: a flat board fixed to a wall or in a frame for holding things, or a ledge of rock under water
core_image: 一块木板钉在墙上，上面排着一列书
scene: 他把书放回架上。 He put the book back on the shelf.
sceneCN: 这里 shelf 是「架子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把书放回架上。

senses.title: Board
senses.definition: a flat board used to hold things
senses.definitionCN: 用来放置物品的平板
senses.example: He put the book back on the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 他把书放回架上。
senses.why: This is the basic furniture sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的家具义项。

senses.title: Shelving unit
senses.definition: a set of shelves in a frame
senses.definitionCN: 框架中的一组搁板
senses.example: The shelf is full of jars.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上摆满了罐子。
senses.why: The board stands for the whole unit.
senses.whyCN: 一块板代指整套架子。

senses.title: Rock ledge
senses.definition: a flat ledge of rock, especially under water
senses.definitionCN: 平坦的岩台，尤指水下的
senses.example: The ship hit a shelf of rock.
senses.exampleCN: 船撞上了岩礁。
senses.why: Nature builds shelves too.
senses.whyCN: 自然也会造出平台。

senses.title: Put aside
senses.definition: left unused or delayed, as in on the shelf
senses.definitionCN: 被闲置或推迟，如 on the shelf
senses.example: The plan is on the shelf for now.
senses.exampleCN: 计划暂时被搁置。
senses.why: Something on a shelf is set aside for later.
senses.whyCN: 放在架上的东西被留待以后。

intro.en: Shelf comes from Middle English shelfe, from Old English scylfe, a ledge.
intro.cn: shelf 源自古英语 scylfe（岩台、搁板），中古英语作 shelfe。

items.en: Scylfe meant a ledge or board.
items.cn: scylfe 意为岩台或搁板。

items.en: Shelfe named a board for holding things.
items.cn: shelfe 指放东西的板。

items.en: Shelf named a rock ledge under water.
items.cn: shelf 指水下的岩台。

items.en: Shelf life named how long goods last.
items.cn: shelf life 指商品的保质期。

items.en: On the shelf meant set aside.
items.cn: on the shelf 意为被搁置。

note.en: Shelf is compared with similar-looking words and with words for ledges and racks.
note.cn: 把 shelf 与形近词以及表示岩台和架子结构的词作比较。

entries.definition: a hard outer case
entries.definitionCN: 壳

entries.definition: a farm animal with wool
entries.definitionCN: 绵羊

entries.definition: to move something
entries.definitionCN: 移动

entries.definition: a narrow flat surface
entries.definitionCN: 壁架

entries.definition: a frame for holding things
entries.definitionCN: 搁物架

entries.definition: a long flat surface in a shop
entries.definitionCN: 柜台

normalIntro.en: A shelf is a flat board that holds things, whether on a wall or under the sea.
normalIntro.cn: shelf 是托住东西的平板，无论在墙上还是在海底。

normal.en: The books are on the top shelf.
normal.cn: 书在顶层架子上。

normal.en: Put the jars on the shelf.
normal.cn: 把罐子放在架子上。

normal.en: The ship struck a rock shelf.
normal.cn: 船撞上了岩礁。

normal.en: The proposal is on the shelf.
normal.cn: 提案被搁置了。

normal.en: Check the shelf life of the milk.
normal.cn: 看看牛奶的保质期。

abstract.en: A shelf holds things without owning them.
abstract.cn: 架子托住东西，却不拥有它们。

abstract.en: Setting something aside can be a decision.
abstract.cn: 把东西搁起来也可以是一种决定。

abstract.en: The sea keeps shelves no one can see.
abstract.cn: 大海保留着无人能见的岩台。

examples.en: He put the book back on the shelf.
examples.cn: 他把书放回架上。

examples.en: The shelf is full of jars.
examples.cn: 架子上摆满了罐子。

examples.en: The ship hit a shelf of rock.
examples.cn: 船撞上了岩礁。

dict_mnemonic.text: shelf 源自古英语 scylfe（岩台、搁板），核心义「伸出的平板」，由家具架引申为水下岩礁与搁置。

root: 源自古英语 scylfe（岩台、搁板），核心义「水平伸出的承托面」。

sensesIntro.en: Shelf means a flat board, a shelving unit, an underwater ledge, or a state of being set aside.
sensesIntro.cn: shelf 意为搁板、架子、水下岩礁或被搁置状态。

core.en: A flat surface that holds things out from a base.
core.cn: 从基座伸出的承托平面。

branches.en: A board holding objects.
branches.cn: 托住物品的板。

branches.en: A whole frame of boards.
branches.cn: 整套框架搁板。

branches.en: A natural rock terrace.
branches.cn: 天然的岩石平台。

branches.en: Something left waiting on a shelf.
branches.cn: 留在架上等待的东西。

branches.en: Holding and postponing share the same board.
branches.cn: 承托与搁置共享同一块板。

intro.en: Shelf builds words for furniture, storage, and delay.
intro.cn: shelf 构成表示家具、储物和延迟的词。

latinIntro.en: Shelf has no Latin ancestor; Latin pluteus, a shelf, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shelf 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 pluteus（搁板）只是语义对应词。

definition_zh: 野生的；荒野的；狂热的；失控的；荒凉的
definition_en: living or growing freely in nature without people, and figuratively uncontrolled, violent or very enthusiastic
core_image: 一片没有篱笆的草坡，风一过草就朝同一个方向倒，中间有一条窄窄的兽径
scene: 山坡上没有篱笆、没有人修的路，只有一条被野兽踩出来的窄径，草随风倒向一边。 Wild horses still run on this island in summer.
sceneCN: 这里 wild 是「野生的」（第 1 个义项：在自然中自由生长或生活、未经人驯养）；句意为夏天这个岛上仍有野马奔跑。没有篱笆的草坡与那条兽径，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 野生的；无人居住的；狂热的；失控的

senses.title: Living free in nature
senses.definition: used of plants and animals that grow or live without being kept or planted by people
senses.definitionCN: 形容未被人饲养或栽种的动植物
senses.example: Wild horses still run on this island in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天这个岛上仍有野马奔跑。
senses.why: The oldest sense is untamed, which is the state of a creature that no one owns or feeds.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是未被驯服，即没有任何人拥有或喂养的状态。

senses.title: Land without people
senses.definition: used of country that is empty, rough and not farmed or built on
senses.definitionCN: 形容空旷、崎岖、未被耕种或建起的土地
senses.example: Beyond the village there are miles of wild hills.
senses.exampleCN: 村子外面是连绵数里的荒山。
senses.why: An untamed creature needs untamed land, so the word covers the ground as well as its inhabitants.
senses.whyCN: 未经驯服的动物需要未经驯服的土地，于是这个词也覆盖了地面。

senses.title: Out of control
senses.definition: used of behaviour, weather or imagination that runs without restraint
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为、天气或想象失去约束地奔流
senses.example: The crowd went wild when the winning goal went in.
senses.exampleCN: 制胜球进门时，人群发狂了。
senses.why: A wild horse cannot be led, and human feeling that cannot be led takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 野马牵不动，而牵不动的人的情绪也用同一个词。

senses.title: Very keen on something
senses.definition: in informal use, extremely enthusiastic about a person or activity
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示对某人或某事极度热衷
senses.example: The children are wild about the new cartoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们对这部新动画片着迷得不行。
senses.why: Enthusiasm without restraint is another way of being untamed, so the word softened into liking.
senses.whyCN: 不知节制的热情也是未驯服的一种，于是这个词软化成喜欢。

senses.title: Rough and inaccurate
senses.definition: used of a guess or a claim that is made without care or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容猜测或断言轻率、没有依据
senses.example: It was only a wild guess, but it turned out right.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是个胡猜，结果竟然猜对了。
senses.why: An arrow shot without aim flies wild, and a guess without aim takes the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 不经瞄准射出的箭会乱飞，不经瞄准的猜测也用这个形容词。

intro.en: Wild comes from Old English wilde, meaning untamed and living in the forest, from a Germanic word for the uncontrolled.
intro.cn: wild 源自古英语 wilde，意为未被驯服、生活在林野之中，其日耳曼语源头与「无约束」有关。

items.en: The root described what was not under human hand, whether a beast or a wood.
items.cn: 这个词根描述不受人手掌控之物，无论野兽还是林子。

items.en: Wilde meant untamed and also described empty, uncultivated land.
items.cn: wilde 表示未被驯服，也描述空旷未耕的土地。

items.en: The word moved from the forest to people, so a wild mood was one without restraint.
items.cn: 这个词从林子移向人，于是 wild mood 指不受约束的情绪。

items.en: Sports writing made go wild the phrase for a crowd losing control.
items.cn: 体育写作让 go wild 成为形容人群失控的说法。

items.en: Casual speech softened it into enthusiasm, as in wild about a band.
items.cn: 口语把它软化为热情，如 wild about a band。

note.en: The first group gathers the closely related wild- words, the second the words for untamed things and land.
note.cn: 第一组收密切相关的 wild- 词族，第二组收表示未驯服之物与土地的词。

entries.definition: Animals and plants living free.
entries.definitionCN: 野生动物

entries.definition: In an uncontrolled way, or very much.
entries.definitionCN: 狂野地；极

entries.definition: Large land left untamed.
entries.definitionCN: 荒野

entries.definition: Broad, differing by one sound.
entries.definitionCN: 宽的

entries.definition: Not made tame or obedient.
entries.definitionCN: 未驯服的

entries.definition: Violent and dangerous in attack.
entries.definitionCN: 凶猛的

entries.definition: Unprocessed, rough and direct.
entries.definitionCN: 未加工的；粗犷的

normalIntro.en: Wild is a short word with a lot of force, so keep the untamed creature and let the other senses grow from it.
normalIntro.cn: wild 很短却很有力，记住那只未驯服的野兽，其他义项都从它长出来。

normal.en: Wild is the opposite of tame, and a tame horse can be led.
normal.cn: wild 与 tame 相对，而驯服的马是能牵走的。

normal.en: Go wild, run wild, wild guess: all have no rein.
normal.cn: go wild、run wild、wild guess：都没有缰绳。

normal.en: Wild about means keen, the same no-rein energy turned to liking.
normal.cn: wild about 表示热衷，是同一股无缰的劲头变成了喜欢。

normal.en: Wildlife and wilderness both start from this one word.
normal.cn: wildlife 与 wilderness 都从这个词出发。

normal.en: Wild differs from wide only in the final sound.
normal.cn: wild 与 wide 只差最后一个音。

abstract.en: Feel grass bend all the way over in one wind.
abstract.cn: 感觉草被一阵风整个压弯。

abstract.en: See a narrow track made by animals, not people.
abstract.cn: 看见一条由动物而非人踩出的小径。

abstract.en: Hear a crowd roaring louder than the whistle.
abstract.cn: 听见人群的吼声比哨声还响。

examples.en: Wild flowers line the path every spring.
examples.cn: 每年春天小路两边都开满野花。

examples.en: The crowd went wild when the singer appeared.
examples.cn: 歌手出现时人群沸腾了。

examples.en: Beyond the wall the land turns wild and rocky.
examples.cn: 墙那边土地变得荒凉多石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪的」——长歪了没人管，就变成野生的了。

root: 日耳曼语词根（不受掌控）→ 古英语 wilde（未驯服、荒芜）→ 中古英语 wild → 现代英语 wild；同族有 wildly、wilderness、wildlife。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a creature no one owns, spreads to land with no people, jumps to feeling without a rein, softens into keen liking, and ends with a guess that has no aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从无人拥有的生物出发，扩展到无人的土地，跳到没有缰绳的情绪，软化为热衷，最后落在没有瞄准的猜测上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fenceless slope with one narrow track worn by animals.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有篱笆的草坡，只有一条兽径。

branches.en: The horses branch: wild horses on the island.
branches.cn: 野马分支：岛上的野马。

branches.en: The hills branch: miles of rough empty land.
branches.cn: 山野分支：连绵数里的荒山。

branches.en: The crowd branch: roaring at the winning goal.
branches.cn: 人群分支：制胜球时的怒吼。

branches.en: The fan branch: children and a new cartoon.
branches.cn: 粉丝分支：孩子与新动画。

branches.en: The guess branch: right by accident.
branches.cn: 猜测分支：碰巧猜对。

intro.en: Wild is a free adjective that builds the -ly adverb, the -ness noun and the older noun wilderness, and it heads compounds such as wildlife.
intro.cn: wild 是自由使用的形容词，可派生 -ly 副词、-ness 名词与较古老的 wilderness，还作为前项构成 wildlife 一类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show the borrowed words for untamed nature.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目展示表示未经驯服之自然的借入词。

items.example: It works as adjective, noun and adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它可作形容词、名词与副词。

items.example: It forms wildly, also meaning very.
The crowd picture in two words.
items.exampleCN: 两个词画出人群的画面。

items.example: It suits children and gardens alike.
items.exampleCN: 它既适合孩子也适合园子。

items.example: The adjective turned noun keeps the land.
items.exampleCN: 形容词转名词后保留了土地之意。

definition_zh: 接受；同意；承认；接纳
definition_en: to take something that is offered, or to agree to something
core_image: 伸手接过别人递来的礼物
scene: 生日会上，女孩伸手接过朋友递来的礼物。 She accepted the gift with a smile.
sceneCN: 这里 accepted 是「接受」（第 1 个义项：收下别人给的东西）；句意为她笑着收下了礼物。

pos.zh: 动词：接受；同意；承认；接纳

senses.title: To take what is offered
senses.definition: to take something that someone offers
senses.definitionCN: 收下别人给予的东西
senses.example: She accepted the gift with a smile.
senses.exampleCN: 她笑着接受了礼物。
senses.why: Accept comes from Latin accipere, to take to oneself, so the first sense is simply taking what is offered.
senses.whyCN: accept 来自拉丁语 accipere「接过来」，本义就是把别人给的东西收下。

senses.title: To agree to a plan
senses.definition: to say yes to a plan or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 对计划或想法表示同意
senses.example: The class accepted the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 全班接受了新规定。
senses.why: Taking something in the mind turns into agreeing with a proposal.
senses.whyCN: 把某物收进心里，就转为对提议表示同意。

senses.title: To admit a fact
senses.definition: to agree that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 同意某事是真的
senses.example: He accepted that he was wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认自己错了。
senses.why: A fact is taken in rather than pushed away, which gives the sense of admitting.
senses.whyCN: 把事实收进来而不是推开，就得到承认的意思。

senses.title: To take someone into a group
senses.definition: to let a person join a group
senses.definitionCN: 让某人加入一个群体
senses.example: The team accepted him as a member.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍接纳他为成员。
senses.why: Taking a person into a group is the social form of taking something offered.
senses.whyCN: 把一个人收进群体，是「收下给予之物」在人际关系上的形式。

intro.en: The recorded history of accept is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 accept 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Accipere meant to take to oneself, and it joined ad- with capere.
items.cn: accipere 意为把东西收到自己这里，由 ad- 与 capere 结合而成。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and it lies behind many English words.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取或抓住，是许多英语词的来源。

items.en: Old French shaped the verb as accepter.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词塑造成 accepter。

items.en: English used accept for taking what is offered.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 accept 指收下所给之物。

items.en: Today it also means agreeing, admitting and letting in.
items.cn: 今天它还表示同意、承认与接纳。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The third person form of the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: The past form of the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的过去式。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of taking or agreeing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指接受或同意的行为。

entries.definition: It stresses getting something that is sent or given.
entries.definitionCN: 强调收到寄来或给予的东西。

entries.definition: It stresses saying yes to a plan or idea.
entries.definitionCN: 强调对计划或想法表示赞同。

entries.definition: It stresses saying that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 强调承认某事为真。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: ac- means to and capere means to take: accept is to take something offered.
normal.cn: ac- 表示向，capere 表示拿：accept 就是把递来的东西接过来。

normal.en: The same family also gives acceptance and acceptable.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 acceptance 与 acceptable。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase accept a gift.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「接受礼物」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of accept in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 accept 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to take something that is offered, or to agree to something.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「接受」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a hand taking a gift that another person offers.
abstract.cn: 想象伸手接过别人递来的礼物。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: She accepted the gift with a smile.
examples.cn: 她笑着接受了礼物。

examples.en: He accepted that he was wrong.
examples.cn: 他承认自己错了。

examples.en: The team accepted him as a member.
examples.cn: 队伍接纳他为成员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞普特」——伸手接过朋友递来的礼物：接受

root: accept 来自拉丁语 accipere「收到自己这里」，由 ad-「向」与 capere「拿」构成，经古法语 accepter 进入英语；英语十四世纪用它指收下所给之物，今天还表示同意、承认与接纳。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of accept grows from one core image: a hand taking a gift that another person offers.
sensesIntro.cn: accept 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：伸手接过别人递来的礼物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand taking a gift that another person offers
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手接过别人递来的礼物

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: To take what is offered.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：接受给予之物。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: To agree to a plan.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：同意某项提议。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: To admit a fact.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：承认某个事实。

branches.en: Sense 04 covers a later use: To take someone into a group.
branches.cn: 义项 04 覆盖再往后的一种用法：接纳某人为成员。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 04 covers the two main uses: To take what is offered / To take someone into a group.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 04 覆盖两个主要用法：接受给予之物、接纳某人为成员。

intro.en: accept can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: accept 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It is a form of ad- used before c.
items.exampleCN: 它是 ad- 在 c 前的变体。

items.example: It comes from capere, meaning to take.
It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

items.example: It turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: 缺席的；不在的；缺乏的；心不在焉的
definition_en: not present in a place, or not existing, or not paying attention
core_image: 教室里空着的座位
scene: 上课铃响后，教室后排有一个空座位。 One pupil was absent from class today.
sceneCN: 这里 absent 是「缺席的」（第 1 个义项：不在场）；句意为今天有一名学生缺课。

pos.zh: 形容词：缺席的；不在的；缺乏的；心不在焉的

senses.title: Not present
senses.definition: not in the place where one should be
senses.definitionCN: 不在本应到场的地方
senses.example: Three pupils were absent today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天有三名学生缺席。
senses.why: Absent comes from Latin absens, being away, and it names the person who is not there.
senses.whyCN: absent 来自拉丁语 absens「不在场」，直接指人没有到场。

senses.title: Missing from a place
senses.definition: not found in a place where it is expected
senses.definitionCN: 在本该出现的地方找不到
senses.example: The old sign is absent from the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上缺少那块旧牌子。
senses.why: The sense of a person away was widened to things that are not where they belong.
senses.whyCN: 把「人不在」扩到事物，就表示某物在该处缺失。

senses.title: Not paying attention
senses.definition: with the mind somewhere else
senses.definitionCN: 心思在别处
senses.example: He wore an absent look in class.
senses.exampleCN: 他在课上显得心不在焉。
senses.why: The body is there but the mind is away, so absent also describes a wandering attention.
senses.whyCN: 人虽在场，心却「不在」，于是 absent 也形容注意力游移。

intro.en: The recorded history of absent is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 absent 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Abesse meant to be away, built from ab- and esse.
items.cn: abesse 意为不在，由 ab- 与 esse 构成。

items.en: Absens was the present participle, meaning being away.
items.cn: absens 是现在分词，意为不在的。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词带向英语。

items.en: English used absent for people and for things that were missing.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 absent 指人不在，也指事物缺少。

items.en: Today it also describes a dreamy, unwatching mind.
items.cn: 今天它也形容走神、不留心的状态。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: A person who is away when expected.

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something without attention.

entries.definition: It stresses that a thing cannot be found.

entries.definition: It stresses that something needed is not there.
entries.definitionCN: 强调需要的东西没有。

definition_zh: 优势；有利条件；好处；利益
definition_en: something that puts a person in a better position or brings a benefit
core_image: 站在高处的人看得更远
scene: 登山比赛中，站在高处的选手看得更远，也走得更快。 High ground gave the team an advantage.
sceneCN: 这里 advantage 是「优势」（第 1 个义项：更有利的位置）；句意为高地给了这支队伍优势。

pos.zh: 名词：优势；有利条件；好处；利益

senses.title: A better position
senses.definition: a condition that puts one ahead of others
senses.definitionCN: 使人处在别人前面的条件
senses.example: Our team has a clear advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队有明显优势。
senses.why: The word comes from a French phrase meaning in front, so the first sense is the better position of being ahead.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自法语短语「在前面」，所以第一义是处在别人前头的优势。

senses.title: A helpful condition
senses.definition: something that helps one do better
senses.definitionCN: 有助于做得更好的事物
senses.example: A quiet room is an advantage for study.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的房间对学习是有利条件。
senses.why: A thing that puts one in front is a helpful condition, which gives the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 能让人处在前头的事物，就是有利条件。

senses.title: A benefit
senses.definition: a good result that something brings
senses.definitionCN: 某事物带来的好结果
senses.example: The plan has many advantages.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划有许多好处。
senses.why: What places one ahead also brings good results, and that is a benefit.
senses.whyCN: 让人处在前头的东西也会带来好结果，这就是好处。

senses.title: To make use of something
senses.definition: used in take advantage of for using a chance
senses.definitionCN: 用于 take advantage of，表示利用机会
senses.example: He took advantage of the free class.
senses.exampleCN: 他利用了那节免费课。
senses.why: Taking a chance that puts one ahead is the everyday phrase take advantage of.
senses.whyCN: 把机会变成自己的前头位置，就是 take advantage of「利用」。
